Exactly what I needed for organizing my disc collection. Super affordable and they do the job perfectly. Can't complain at this price.
Picked this up to split my monitor signal and it handles 1080p flawlessly with zero lag. Plug and play, no setup needed.
Perfect for students or anyone needing extra storage. Plugged it in and it worked instantly. Super quiet and takes up barely any space on my desk.
Solid cord for hooking up my printer. The braided jacket feels durable and connections stay tight. Only wish it came in a longer size.
Can't beat the price on these. Sound comes through clean with no static, and the cable feels sturdy. Picked up two and both work flawlessly.
Been using these daily for about six months now and they're still going strong. Cables haven't frayed or loosened at all. Solid buy.
Perfect backup charger for my office desk. Charges just as fast as the one that came with my laptop. Cable feels sturdy and the connector fits snugly. Very happy.
Arrived two days early in secure packaging. Opened it up and was genuinely surprised by the solid build quality. Glides smoothly across my phone screen right away.
Does exactly what I needed without breaking the bank. Build quality is just okay, but honestly fine for the price. Perfect for anyone wanting a basic, no-frills option.
Perfect little PC for the kids' homework station. Fast startup, surprisingly capable for the price. Would definitely recommend to anyone needing a basic secondary computer.
Swapped out the dead speakers in my Silverado and these dropped right in. Sound is way better than stock, nice and crisp. Super happy with the upgrade.
Setup took maybe five minutes and the signal reaches every corner of my house. Blazing fast speeds on both bands. No drops in three months.
Worked fine for about three weeks, then the plastic housing cracked and the connection got super loose. Completely stopped charging after a month. Cheaply made.
Didn't expect much for the price but figured I'd try it. Honestly performs better than units costing twice as much. Solid construction and surprisingly accurate readings.
Arrived two days early, nicely boxed with foam padding. Feels super solid straight out of the package. Hung my 22-inch monitor in the RV no problem.
Can't believe how well this works for under nine bucks. Does exactly what it claims and feels way more expensive than it is. Totally worth every penny.
Honestly can't beat these for what they cost. Paired instantly with my phone, sound is surprisingly clear, and the ear hooks stay put during workouts. Great budget pick.
Plug and play on my Mac, no drivers needed. Transfer speeds are surprisingly fast for such a cheap drive. Picked up two more after testing the first one.
Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this thing punches way above its weight. RouterOS has every feature I needed and then some. Totally exceeded my expectations.
Honestly didn't expect much at this price point, but this thing glides without any stutter. Feels way more solid than I thought it would. Totally surprised.
Bought this 4TB for my PC build and it's been flawless. Perfect for gamers and content creators needing serious storage. Runs quiet and stays cool. Totally worth it.
Had this drive over two years now, tossed it in my bag constantly. Still reads discs flawlessly. Solid little workhorse for cheap.
Bought this as a backup for my Toshiba and it's been perfect. Charges fast, packs small for travel, and stays cool even after hours of use. Totally worth it.
Arrived two days early in secure packaging with no damage. Pulled it out and immediately noticed how solid everything feels. Connectors fit snugly. Really impressed for the price.
Arrived two days early, double-boxed and well protected. Unboxed it and was immediately impressed with the build quality. Plugged it in and had it running in minutes. Fantastic monitor.
Hooked this up to get an old DVD player running through my coax TV setup. Picture quality is decent, not perfect, but totally watchable. Setup took maybe five minutes. Does what I needed it to do.
Couldn't believe the quality for what I paid. Replaced my blown door speakers and the clarity is night and day. Solid bass response too. Definitely worth every penny.
Decent battery for the price. Holds a charge reasonably well for day-to-day shooting, but drains noticeably fast in cold weather. Fine as a backup, just don't rely on it for long trips.
Sound is decent for the price but the bass really lacks punch. I expected more from the subwoofer. Fine for casual listening, but not great for movies or loud music.
Solid tablet for what I paid. Screen is bright enough and battery gets through most of the day. Not the fastest but totally fine for kids' apps and videos.
Worked fine for the first couple months of occasional use, then one of the plastic joints cracked from normal setup. Still functions but feels flimsy now. Wouldn't trust it long-term.
Had this hooked up to my living room setup for about eight months now and it's taken a beating. Switches between my PC and console without issues. Wish the remote was backlit though.
Arrived two days early in sturdy packaging with solid anti-static protection. Popped it into my slim desktop, loaded the drivers, and had dual screens running in under ten minutes.
Bought this as a backup for my XC tripod and honestly the quality is just as good as the original. At this price, it's a no-brainer. Fits perfectly and works like a charm.
Had this about six months now and it's held up great. Dropped my Kindle twice and no damage to either the device or the case. Snug fit, nice grip, still looks brand new.
Swapped out my old dead battery for this one and my laptop runs a solid three hours unplugged now. Snapped right in with no issues. Genuinely impressed for the price.

Got these for my daily train commute and they're perfect. Blocks out noise surprisingly well without being bulky. Battery lasts all week. Would definitely recommend to anyone needing solid everyday headphones on a budget.
Arrived in a damaged box with no protective padding. The screen had a small scratch right out of the package. Setup was frustrating and the band feels flimsy. Expected better quality for the price.

Arrived two days early in a sturdy box with no damage. Opened it up and was immediately impressed by the build quality, feels solid and well-made. Setup took maybe five minutes. So glad I pulled the trigger on this one.

Picked this up to connect my older external drives to my MacBook Air and the speeds are honestly impressive. Zero setup required, just plugged it in and it worked. Highly recommend it to anyone still sitting on eSATA enclosures.
Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this thing handles my external drive, keyboard, and mouse without breaking a sweat. Way faster than my old one. Plug and play right out of the box.
Had this for about six months now. Dropped it off my desk twice and it still fires right up, so it's tough. Magnification is just okay though, and the LED gets warm on longer sessions.

Thought this would feel cheap for the price but it's surprisingly solid. Way more responsive than the bigger Logitech one I replaced. Battery lasts forever and the trackpad actually works well. Exceeded my expectations for a couch controller.

Me sorprendio el bajo tan potente, la verdad esperaba algo mas plano. La bateria me dura bastante y suenan muy bien. Solo que despues de un rato largo te calientan las orejas. En general cumplen bien.

Decent budget flash for someone just learning off-camera lighting. Works fine in manual mode but the lack of high-speed sync really limits outdoor use. I'd recommend it to beginners or hobbyists on a tight budget, but pros should look elsewhere.

Expected way more based on the description. Setup took forever and the connection kept dropping on me. My old USB hub honestly performs better than this thing. Pretty disappointing for the price point. It's gathering dust now.

Got this to run ethernet from my router to my PC across the house. The snagless boots are a nice touch, makes unplugging way easier when I'm swapping stuff around. Solid connection, no drops, gigabit speeds no problem.

The manual focus on this Rokinon is buttery smooth and the focus peaking on my Sony makes it a breeze to nail sharp shots. Corner sharpness wide open genuinely surprised me for the price. Solid build, no complaints at all.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but these little remotes have been rock solid. Reaching our secondary bedroom setup from about 60 feet away through two walls with zero lag. Way better range than I anticipated. Totally worth it.

Needed this to rip my old CD collection to my PC. Read speeds are decent and it handled scratched discs better than I expected. The USB cable is annoyingly short though, had to use an extension cord to reach my tower.

Total waste of money. Expected this to plug and play like other adapters I've used, but it constantly nags for a driver disk. My laptop doesn't even have a disc drive. Completely useless. Don't bother.

Arrived two days early in solid packaging with no dents on the box. Plugged it in, called my provider to activate, and was online within ten minutes. Speeds are noticeably faster than the old rental. Great little modem so far.

Arrived two days early in secure packaging with no dents. Opened the box and was immediately impressed by how solid it feels. Snapped a few test shots right away and the clarity blew me away. Totally worth it.

Got these for trail running and they're perfect for that. Music comes through decently while keeping me aware of my surroundings. Wouldn't pick them for quiet listening at home, but for anyone who needs situational awareness outdoors, these do the job well.

Got these expecting average sound for the price, but they genuinely surprised me. The highs are sharp and the low end fills the room way better than my old pair. Not perfect at max volume, but solid for what I paid.

Been using this daily for about three weeks now and honestly it's exceeded my expectations. Battery easily lasts me through a full workday plus evening gym sessions. Notifications sync perfectly with my phone and the screen looks great outdoors. Really glad I picked this up.

Total waste of money. Plugged it into my PS4 and it was super slow from day one. Kept freezing during saves and eventually corrupted all my data. Had to reformat twice in three months. Threw it in the trash yesterday. Avoid at all costs.

Arrived two days early in a sturdy box with no dents. Pulled it out and was surprised by how solid it feels, not flimsy at all. The buttons have a nice click to them. Still figuring out all the features, but so far I'm impressed with the build quality.

Been using this daily for about six months now and it's held up great. Sweat, rain, showers, still ticking. Battery still gets me through a full week. Syncing is reliable and the band hasn't cracked or stretched out. Solid little tracker for the price.

Put these in the back of my Civic and wow, what a difference. The highs are crisp and the bass punches way harder than I expected for the cost. For the money, you'd be hard pressed to find anything that sounds this clean. Totally worth every penny.

Solid adapter for the price. Connected my Galaxy Note to my LG flat screen without any issues, plug and play, no fiddling required. Picture quality is decent, though audio sync can lag slightly on longer cables. Still, it gets the job done reliably for presentations and movie nights.

Looked decent at first but after about three weeks the edges started peeling up on their own. Now there's a crack running across the middle and I haven't even dropped my phone. Expected way better longevity for the price. Going back to my usual brand.

Perfect for my Pi 4 setup. The individual port power switching is what sold me, I can cut power to a hung external drive without yanking cables or rebooting everything. Handles my SSD and fan simultaneously without breaking a sweat. Build quality feels solid for the price.

Got this for my son's school Chromebook and it's been a lifesaver. Fits snug, the strap makes carrying easy, and there's room for the charger inside. For the price, you really can't beat it. Held up great after three months of kid abuse.

Shipped fast in a plain padded mailer, no issues. The couplers feel solid for the price, with clean gold contacts and a tight connection between my cables. Red/white markings are easy to spot. Ran a turntable through two joined cables, no signal loss. Happy with these.

Worked fine for maybe two weeks then the mic just cut out completely during a shoot. The shoe mount is super flimsy too and wobbles constantly on my hot shoe. Really disappointing because the pickup pattern actually sounded decent while it lasted.

Total waste of money. The hard shell cracked within two days of normal use, and the keyboard skin doesn't even stay put while typing. You'd expect better quality for thirty bucks. Cheap materials and flimsy construction throughout. Don't bother, spend a little more on something that actually holds up.

Picked this up last month for a trip and it handled everything I threw at it. Photos come out crisp and the menu system is intuitive enough that I didn't need the manual. Battery gets me through a full day of shooting. Tripod feels flimsy but the camera body itself is solid. Glad I went with this one.

Needed to connect a third display to my GTX 1070 and passive adapters kept giving me a black screen. Picked this up and it worked instantly with zero configuration. If you're running multiple monitors off a card with limited ports, this is exactly what you need.

Couldn't believe the quality for what I paid. Local shops wanted triple the price for the exact same part. Took maybe ten minutes to install and it's been running flawlessly since. Honestly wasn't expecting much at this price point but totally proved me wrong.

Arrived two days early in a sturdy box with proper bubble wrap. Popped it on my full-spectrum converted DSLR right away and the colors looked normal instantly without any custom white balance fiddling. Build quality feels solid for the price. Very impressed so far.

Arrived quickly in a padded mailer, no damage. First impression out of the box was nice, the fabric feels premium and the magnet flap clicks securely. But it's pretty tight getting my Surface in, and I can't leave the type cover attached. Decent enough for what I paid, just wish it had more room.

Got this for my daughter's online classes and it's been fantastic. Setup took minutes and the screen looks sharp. She watches videos, plays educational games, and types up assignments without any lag. Battery easily lasts the whole school day. For the price, I'm genuinely impressed with the quality.

Grabbed this bundle for my Coolpix and honestly the UV glass alone justifies the price. The ND filters knock down glare nicely on bright days without wrecking color. Threaded on smooth, no binding. Carry pouch is basic but functional. Hard to beat for the money if you shoot outdoors.

Honestly thought the cable would feel flimsy for the price but it's surprisingly sturdy and the locking mechanism clicks in securely. Fits my Dell perfectly. Knocked off a star because it's a bit shorter than I pictured, so measure your setup first. Overall does exactly what it says though.

I'm a wedding videographer and needed a reliable way to feed audio from my mixer straight into my camera without tangled cables. This little transmitter handles it flawlessly. Zero lag, clean signal. Highly recommend to any solo run-and-gun shooter who needs professional audio without a sound guy tagging along.

Lost my original cap and needed a quick replacement. This one snaps on perfectly and fits snug with no wiggle. No issues with it falling off while the camera's bouncing around in my bag. Genuinely impressed with the build quality for the price. Arrived fast and does the job right.

Honestly expected these to be flimsier given how cheap they were, but the plastic is surprisingly rigid and the nails went into drywall without bending. They hold my speaker wire tight against the baseboard with no slipping. Wish the clip opening was a hair wider for thicker cables, but for the price, totally solid.

Been using this adapter daily for about eight months now and it's held up great. I travel for work constantly so it gets tossed in my bag and yanked around quite a bit. Cable is still solid with no fraying and connection stays reliable. Build quality genuinely surprised me for the price.

Arrived a day late and the box was pretty banged up. Figured I'd try it anyway since it paired with my phone quickly. But the screen is super dim and the touch response is laggy. Feels cheap in hand too. Definitely not worth what they're asking. Sending it back.

Can't beat this for the price. Grabbed the blue version and it fits my iPod Touch perfectly with no wobbling. Buttons stay easy to press and the grip feels solid in hand. Dropped it twice already with zero damage to my device. Seriously, for this cheap you can't go wrong.

Pretty solid fan filter for the price. Does what it's supposed to and keeps the dust buildup manageable. Had to get a little creative with the mounting since my case has an unusual front setup, but nothing too frustrating. Airflow seems unaffected and my temps haven't changed. Wish it came in more sizes but overall glad I grabbed it.

Grabbed a couple of these for my home studio setup and honestly they perform just as well as the name brands costing three times more. Solid grip, no slippage once dialed in. If you're a podcaster or musician on a budget, these are a no-brainer. Perfect for anyone upgrading their gear without breaking the bank.

Arrived two days late in a slightly crushed box, though the headphones inside were fine. First impression out of the box was decent build quality for the price, but the clamping force is pretty intense right away. Sound is okay for casual listening but nothing jumped out at me as special. Still deciding whether to keep them.

Been using this on job sites for about six months now and it's held up great. Dropped it in a puddle last week and every card stayed perfectly dry. The latch still clicks shut tight with no issues. Holds my essential cards securely, though I do wish it fit a couple more. Solid build for the money.

Been using this cable daily for about six months now and it's held up great. I run it across my studio floor and step on it constantly. No crackling, no loose connections, still sounds clean. The connectors are solid and the jacket hasn't split. Can't ask for more at this price.

Bought this on a whim and it's become my go-to tool around the house. I've opened dozens of packages, cut zip ties, stripped some wire, and even used it for light pruning in the garden. Still holds an edge pretty well. I'd definitely recommend it to anyone who does a lot of DIY projects or just wants a solid everyday blade within reach. Great value for the price.

Bought this for my older MacBook and it does the job. The keys feel decent and it paired up without any hassle. Sometimes the light cuts out but typing wakes it right back up, not a big deal for me. Would definitely recommend to anyone still rocking an older Mac who needs a simple wireless keyboard without spending a fortune.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price, but these little drives have been a pleasant surprise. I've been moving large video files back and forth daily and the transfer speeds hold up way better than the pricier brand I replaced. Build feels sturdy too, not flimsy like some cheap ones I've tried. Definitely exceeding what I paid for them.

Arrived in a flimsy envelope with barely any padding, so the box was pretty banged up. Surprisingly the stand itself was fine. First impression out of the box is that it feels a bit light and the hinges seem a little stiff out of the box. It holds my 10" iPad okay but anything smaller feels wobbly and off-balance. Decent enough for the price but nothing special.

Picked this up last month and honestly it completely changed how I shoot. The autofocus is ridiculously fast, grabs my kids running around no problem. Image quality straight out of camera is stunning. Battery gets me through a full day of casual shooting which surprised me. Coming from an older entry level body, this feels like a massive leap. Totally worth every penny.

Arrived two days early in secure packaging with no damage at all. Plugged them right in and was genuinely surprised by how heavy and well-made they feel. The sound filled my home office instantly with clear highs and decent bass. For the price, these punch way above their weight. Really happy with this purchase so far.

Picked this up on a whim and honestly couldn't be happier. Connected my old Klipsch desktop speakers and streamed Spotify from my iPhone, super clean signal with zero static. If you're sitting at a desk every day like me and want decent audio without dropping hundreds on a new setup, this is a total no-brainer. Perfect for work-from-home folks.

Arrived quickly but the box was pretty beat up and the player was just loose inside with minimal padding. Surprisingly it still worked fine. Sound is decent for the price and setup took about two minutes. Feels a little flimsy and lighter than expected, but it plays CDs without skipping so far. Not bad for what I paid, just wish they'd pack it better.

Arrived thrown in a plain padded envelope with zero instructions or packaging. The protector itself had a visible crease down the middle right out of the envelope. Tried lining it up anyway and the adhesive side was already collecting dust before I even peeled the second layer. Impossible to get a clean seal. Total garbage from the moment I opened the mailer. Don't bother.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this thing blew me away. The metal panels feel solid with zero flex and everything lined up perfectly during assembly. Cable management was way easier than my last case, tons of clearance behind the motherboard tray. The stock fans move serious air without sounding like a jet engine. Way better build quality than I anticipated.

Got this up on my chimney last weekend without any hassle. The build quality is solid and it does exactly what it's supposed to do. If you're reasonably handy with basic tools, you'll have no problems flying solo on the install. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone with an accessible roof who wants a reliable solution without paying someone else to do it. Great value for the price.

Bought this for my garage workshop and the signal reaches about 30 feet before cutting out. Sound quality is fine for podcasts but music sounds flat and muffled. I'd only recommend this to someone who needs a basic transmitter for casual listening in a small space, not for anyone wanting decent audio. For the price it's acceptable, just don't expect much.

Bought this for my desk setup and honestly it's been nothing but frustrating. The legs are super flimsy and wobble constantly, so I can't even use it for video calls without everything shaking. The mount scratched the side of my case pretty badly too. It felt like it was going to snap my phone in half every time I put it in. Spend a few extra bucks on something better built. Total waste.

Arrived two days early in solid packaging with no dents on the box. Everything inside was neatly organized and the hardware felt surprisingly heavy-duty for the price. The included bubble level was a nice touch. I was nervous about hanging my 55-inch but the build quality instantly put me at ease. Hardware sorted into labeled bags which saved me time. Mounting bracket looks clean on the wall too.

I bought this SMC router about two years ago for our farmhouse, and it pushes a solid connection to the barn office roughly 300 feet away. Setup took maybe twenty minutes. Occasionally needs a reboot after a power flicker, but that's minor. If you're running a small business or need coverage across a large property without spending a fortune on mesh gear, this is exactly what you want. Recommended.

Got the variety pack since I never know which size will work with my Powerbeats. The small ones were a bust but the large fit snug and create a decent seal. Sound isolation improved noticeably during my morning runs and they don't budge when I sweat. Knocking off a star because the medium pair felt a bit flimsy and tore after two weeks. Overall though, solid replacement tips for the price.

Box arrived half crushed and the antenna was just loose inside with no padding. The plastic housing already had a crack near the base when I pulled it out. Hooked it up anyway and honestly didn't notice much difference over the cheap dipole I was already using. Feels flimsy and cheaply made for the price. Disappointed right out of the gate. Sending it back.

Arrived two days early in a compact, no-frills package with all 50 straps neatly bundled together. First impression was solid, the material feels durable and the hook-and-loop grip is surprisingly strong right out of the gate. I tested one on a thick power strip cable and it held firm without slipping. Knocking off a star because the ends fray slightly when you pull them tight. Still, great value for cable management.

Took this little speaker on a week-long camping trip and it handled everything I threw at it. Got knocked around in my backpack, sat out in light rain, and still played perfectly. The bass is surprisingly punchy for something this compact, and battery life lasted most of the trip on a single charge. Paired instantly with my phone every time. Honestly sounds better than speakers costing twice as much. Can't beat it for the price.

Arrived two days early in a sturdy box with plenty of padding, so no concerns about damage in transit. Popped it into my desktop and Windows found it right away without needing the included disc. Signal strength sits around four bars consistently through two walls. Not the fastest speeds I've ever seen, but it gets the job done for browsing and streaming. Solid little card for what it costs. Docking one star just because the antenna feels a bit flimsy.

Bought this for my Galaxy Tab and it does the job if you just need basic typing on the go. The keys feel decent for the size and battery lasts a while. That said, the fit is slightly loose and the hinge already shows wear after two weeks of normal use. I'd recommend this for light users or kids who occasionally need a keyboard, but if you're typing daily for work, spend more on something sturdier. It's okay for the price.

Picked this up before a trip to Yellowstone and the zoom on this thing blew me away. Got crisp, detailed shots of bison from what felt like a mile away. Way better than my old point-and-shoot. The menu takes a little getting used to but once you figure it out, it's smooth sailing. Definitely worth the money if you want great photos without hauling around a bunch of lenses.

For the price this is honestly a solid buy. Build quality is decent and it pairs fine with my GoPro 11. The screen is bright enough for outdoor framing and getting shots lined up, which is mainly what I bought it for. Just know there's noticeable delay in the feed, so tracking fast motion is pretty frustrating. Overall though, can't complain too much given what it costs compared to name brand monitors.

Got this for my warehouse and it does the job, but man is this thing bulky. Took up half my shelf space. Picture quality on my monitor looks pretty dated compared to newer systems. The mobile app works but switching through camera groups gets tedious fast. I'd recommend this to someone who just needs basic coverage on a budget and doesn't care about sleek design or HD clarity. Not ideal for anyone wanting modern features.

Got this backup cam setup for my older Civic and honestly can't believe how little I paid. The video feed is sharp during the day and decent at night too. Ran all the wiring myself in maybe two hours with basic tools. The monitor is compact enough to mount anywhere without being obtrusive. Sure it's not top of the line but it does exactly what it needs to do. Hard to beat at this price point.

Arrived two days early in solid packaging with no damage to the box. Pulled it out and was surprised by the clean design, looks way better in person than the photos. Setup took maybe three minutes and the buttons actually make sense for once. Display is bright but not blinding at night. First morning using it and the wake-up chime is smooth, not jarring. Really happy with this purchase so far.

Picked this up to adapt my 67mm polarizer onto a 72mm lens and it does the job without any vignetting in my shots. Build quality is decent, nothing premium but threads are clean and it seats properly. I'd recommend this to anyone doing a single size bump. If you're trying to bridge a massive gap like 82mm down to 52mm, maybe look elsewhere because stacking gets bulky fast. Solid value for straightforward step-down needs.

Needed to swap out the battery on an old iPad mini and these did the trick without any hassle. The variety of bit sizes is impressive, I found the exact pentalobe and Phillips heads I needed right away. The magnetic tips hold screws firmly so nothing rolls off the table. Case keeps everything organized and compact. For the price, you really can't go wrong having this around the house. Definitely recommend for anyone who likes doing their own repairs.

Arrived two days early in a sturdy box with no damage at all. Everything was neatly secured inside with molded plastic, which I appreciated. Setup took maybe five minutes, just plugged in the USB receiver and both pieces connected instantly. The keys feel solid and the mouse has a nice weight to it. Only minor gripe is the mouse is a bit smaller than I expected. Overall, really happy with this purchase so far for the price.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but these genuinely surprised me. The bass is way deeper than my old Sony pair and they stay put during runs which was my main worry. Cord feels thick enough to survive daily commute tangles. Sound isolation is solid too, can barely hear the bus engine. For what they cost I figured I'd be replacing them in a month but going strong after six weeks. Grabbed a backup pair just in case.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this little speaker blew me away. The bass is way deeper than my old JBL and it gets surprisingly loud without distorting. Took it on a kayak trip last weekend and it survived getting splashed repeatedly. Battery lasted the entire six hours we were out. Connects to my phone automatically every time I turn it on. Way better quality than I thought I'd be getting at this price point.

Got this on sale and honestly it's worth every penny. Slides right into my laptop without any fuss and the transfer speeds are way faster than the cheapo ones I've bought before. The rubberized casing gives me confidence tossing it in my bag every day. I've already filled up about half the drive with backup files and zero issues so far. Can't find anything else this tough at this price point.

Arrived in a padded envelope with the box completely crushed. One corner was split open and the earbuds were halfway falling out. Plugged them in anyway and the sound was super tinny with barely any bass. The cord feels flimsy and tangles instantly. Didn't even bother testing them longer than a few minutes. Already boxed them back up for a return. Don't waste your time on these, spend a little more for something better.

Honestly didn't think a power supply would be worth this much money, but I was wrong. Came from a budget unit and the difference is night and day. Voltages barely fluctuate under heavy load according to my multimeter readings. The software monitoring is way more detailed than I expected, you can see exactly what each rail is pulling in real time. Fan basically never spins up during normal gaming sessions. Only knocks half a star because the cables are pretty stiff, but performance is flawless.

Showed up a day early in a sturdy box with zero damage. Really impressed right out of the bag, the material feels premium and the overall build quality is solid. The laptop section is nicely padded and the main compartment swallows everything I need for work. Side pockets are a little awkward to reach but not a dealbreaker. Comfortable on the shoulders even loaded up. Been using it two weeks now and no complaints. Would definitely buy again.

Total waste of money. Mounted this on my kayak frame for recording trips and it seemed decent at first. After about four outings the plastic around the mount started cracking and the whole thing became loose and wobbly. Eventually the connection point just snapped clean off while I was driving to the ramp. I babied this thing too, always took it down after each use and kept it in my tackle box. For the price you'd expect something that holds up better than cheap dollar store junk. Avoid this one.

Sound quality is solid for the price, crisp highs and decent bass that doesn't get muddy at higher volumes. Battery life gets me through a full week of gym sessions without needing a charge. That said, the fit is hit or miss. They kept slipping out during sprints, and the rubber tips don't have enough grip. I'd recommend these to casual listeners or anyone using them at a desk, but runners with smaller ears should probably look elsewhere. Great audio, just not the most secure fit for active use.

Got this for my brother about six months ago and the disc has been through heavy play sessions since. No scratches or loading issues at all, which surprised me because he's not gentle with his games. The case held up fine too. Gameplay itself is solid with nice set pieces and decent combat. Took off a star because some of the climbing sections feel repetitive after a while. Overall a worthwhile pickup that stands up to regular use without falling apart on you.

For the price, you really can't complain. I grabbed this for my Dell 15.6 inch and everything slides in perfectly with breathing room for the charger, mouse, and a thin notebook. The shoulder strap is surprisingly comfortable even when the bag is loaded up, and the material feels way more expensive than what I paid. My only minor gripe is the front pocket could be a bit roomier for cables and dongles. Still, solid build quality and excellent protection for budget shoppers. Definitely recommend it.

Had this on my 15" MacBook Pro for about eight months now and it's held up incredibly well. I toss my laptop in a backpack daily and the edges are still completely intact with no cracking or warping. The matte finish barely shows wear despite constant handling. Snapped on tight from day one and hasn't loosened up at all. Dropped it once from desk height and the case absorbed the impact with zero damage to the laptop underneath. Worth every penny for the protection alone.

Got this for my garage workshop and honestly can't believe how good the picture looks for what I paid. Colors are bright and the 720p resolution is plenty sharp at this size. Hooked up a cheap antenna and pulled in all the local channels without any fuss. The built-in speakers aren't great but that's pretty standard at this price point. I ran a cable to an old soundbar I had laying around and now it sounds solid. For a budget bedroom or garage setup, you really can't go wrong here.

Bought this for an older desktop that didn't have built-in Bluetooth. Popped it into a USB port and Windows 10 recognized it immediately, no driver CD needed. Paired my wireless headphones and a speaker in under a minute with zero lag or dropouts. The range is surprisingly good, I can walk into the next room about 20 feet away and the connection stays solid. For the price, this little adapter completely solved my problem. Highly recommend if you need to add Bluetooth capability to any machine quickly and cheaply.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this little speaker punches way above its weight. Sound is surprisingly clear and fills my whole bathroom without any distortion, even at higher volumes. Pairs fast every time and the battery has lasted over two weeks of daily use. Suction cup actually stays put on wet tile, which was my biggest worry. Way better than the cheap ones I've tried before that barely lasted a month. Totally exceeded what I thought I was getting.

Got this setup about a month ago for some indoor portrait work and I've been pretty impressed overall. The softboxes and snoots give you tons of creative options without needing to invest hundreds in name brand gear. Assembly takes some getting used to and the mounting brackets feel a little flimsy, so I'm careful when attaching heavier modifiers. Once everything is secured though, it stays put through a full session. The carry case is a nice bonus and holds all the pieces snugly. For anyone wanting to experiment with speedlight shaping, this covers all the basics without breaking the bank.

I've been using this enclosure daily for about eight months now and it's held up surprisingly well. I toss it in my backpack constantly and the aluminum casing still looks practically new with no dents or scratches. The USB connection fits snugly and I haven't had any dropouts unlike cheaper enclosures I've tried before. Transfer speeds are solid for my backup drives. Only complaint is the included cable could be a bit longer, but that's minor. For the price this thing is built to last and does exactly what you need it to.

Bought these on a whim after returning a pair of Sonys that hurt my ears. So glad I made the switch. The cushioning on these is super comfortable, I can wear them for a three hour work session and forget they're even on my head. Sound is rich and warm without being muddy. Bass hits clean, not boomy. I mostly listen to jazz and podcasts, and voices come through crystal clear. The cord is plenty long for desk use. For the money, honestly not sure you can do better. Grabbed a second pair for my wife.

Bought this for our bedroom about six weeks ago and overall I'm pretty happy with it. The picture quality is sharp and colors pop nicely, especially for the price point. Setup took maybe fifteen minutes and connecting to WiFi was painless. The smart features work smoothly without lag, which was a pleasant surprise coming from an older Samsung that took forever to load apps. My only gripe is the speakers feel underwhelming during movies, so I grabbed a cheap soundbar and that fixed it completely. Would definitely recommend to anyone shopping on a budget.

Picked these up for cheap and figured I'd give them a shot. The audio quality isn't terrible for the price, mids get a little muddy but they get loud enough. My main issue is the cable noise. Any movement transfers straight into your ears, so using these while walking or working out is basically impossible unless you clip the cord down somehow. The right side quit on me after about two months of pretty light use, just sitting at my desk. For ten dollars I wasn't expecting amazing build quality, but I thought they'd last longer than that. Wouldn't really recommend spending even that much.

Picked this up for camping and it's been surprisingly handy. The reception is decent once you fiddle with the antenna position, and the built-in speaker gets loud enough for a small group. Picture quality is what you'd expect at this price, nothing fancy but totally watchable. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who needs a portable TV for outdoor trips, tailgating, or keeping in the garage. Just know you'll want to invest in a good set of rechargeables since it eats through standard AAs pretty fast on full brightness. Solid little unit overall.

Bought these as my first real upgrade from cheap earbuds and honestly I'm blown away. The clarity is incredible -- I'm hearing background instruments in songs I've listened to hundreds of times. They clamp pretty tight out of the box but loosen up after a week or so of use. The padding on the cups feels luxurious and doesn't make my ears sweat like other closed-backs I've tried. I'd specifically recommend these to anyone getting into audiophile gear without wanting to drop hundreds. Great for students, gamers, or anyone wanting serious sound on a budget.

I bought this for my kid's iPad after going through three cheaper cases that all cracked within weeks. This one is on another level entirely. The dual-layer design really works, hard shell inside, soft rubber outside. Every port has a flap keeping dust out, and the screen protector sits flush without interfering with touch sensitivity. My son has dropped it on hardwood twice now with zero damage. If you've got children using an iPad 2 or 3, don't bother with anything else. Honestly even adults who are rough on their tablets should grab one. You honestly can't beat this level of protection for what they're charging.

For the price, this little light box is hard to beat. I use it for listing small electronics and jewelry online, and the photos come out looking professional. The LED strips are bright and evenly distributed, though the color temperature seems slightly cool even on the warm setting. It folds up nicely into the carrying case, which is great since my desk space is limited. The backdrops are a bit thin and wrinkle easily, so I had to iron mine carefully. Still, for budget product photography, it gets the job done well.

The box showed up looking like somebody played soccer with it. Both end caps were crushed and the spool itself had dents in the metal. No bubble wrap, no padding at all, just a label slapped on the manufacturer's box. I pulled out a section to test and honestly the whole thing feels cheap. The connectors are loose and the outer jacket has a weird waxy residue on it. Didn't even bother hooking it up after seeing how flimsy everything felt. For what this costs you'd expect at least decent packaging. Returning it today, total waste of time.

I wasn't expecting much for the price, honestly figured I'd be returning it within a week. Man was I wrong. This little thing punches way above its weight class. Image quality is sharp, low light performance is better than cameras I've paid triple for. I took it on a weekend trip to the coast and the battery lasted two full days of constant shooting. The menu took maybe ten minutes to figure out and the controls feel solid, not cheap like I assumed they would. Fits in my jacket pocket which was the whole point. Definitely exceeded what I thought I was getting.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price, but this little camera blew me away. My old point-and-shoot took forever to capture a shot, so I kept missing moments with my kids. This one fires almost instantly, and the face-tracking feature locks onto my daughter even when she's running around. Photos come out crisp with accurate colors, way better than my phone. The blue finish looks sharp, and it genuinely fits in my jeans pocket. I was nervous about downsizing from a bulkier model, but no regrets at all. Exceeded every expectation I had and then some.

I've had this player for about three weeks now and I'm mostly happy with it. The Rhapsody integration is seamless, plugged it in, synced my library, and was good to go in minutes. That alone makes it worth the price for me since I burn through a lot of music every month. Battery life is decent, maybe 12 hours of continuous playback. My one real complaint is the scroll wheel feels a little mushy compared to the click wheel on my old Nano. Sometimes it registers a tap when I'm trying to scroll. Takes some getting used to but manageable once you adjust your grip.

I've had these for about eight months now and they're still going strong. I'm rough on earbuds, stuff them in pockets, yank the cord, use them daily at the gym, and most don't last past two months. These have taken everything I've thrown at them without any connection issues or sound degradation in one side. The cable has held up way better than the tangle-prone ones I've had before. Sound is great across all types of music, really clear with punchy bass that doesn't muddy the vocals. For the price, I'm genuinely impressed. Already recommended them to two coworkers who are equally happy.

Ordered this Tuesday and it was at my door by Thursday afternoon. Box arrived in great shape, no dents or crushed corners, and the keyboard itself was tucked inside a fitted foam shell so nothing was rattling around. Pulled it out, plugged it in, and was typing within thirty seconds. The keys feel incredible right away, super responsive with just the right amount of travel. Way more solid than the last two brands I went through. Layout is intuitive and the build quality immediately screams premium. Honestly wish I'd skipped the cheaper ones and just started here. Already thinking about grabbing a second one for my desk at work.

Ordered this for a trip to Costa Rica and it arrived two days earlier than expected. Box was well-protected with air pillows and the camera was snug inside its retail packaging. Popped in the SD card and battery, and it powered right up immediately. The build feels solid despite how light it is, and the screen is bright and crisp. Took a few test shots around the house and the color reproduction blew me away, especially for something this compact. Menu navigation is intuitive enough that I didn't need the manual. Really impressed so far and can't wait to put it through its paces on vacation.

Bought this to connect my work laptop to an older Dell monitor that only has DVI input. Set it up in seconds and it worked immediately with no drivers or fiddling around. The picture quality is sharp with no flickering or signal drops, which I was worried about since my monitor is 1080p. The cable feels sturdy and the connectors fit snugly into both ports without any wobbling. Length is perfect for my desk setup too. Definitely cheaper than buying a new monitor just to get HDMI. Been using it daily for about two months now with zero issues. Highly recommend if you need a reliable adapter cable.

Honestly didn't expect much from something this cheap, but it's been a lifesaver. My new laptop only has USB C ports and I still have a bunch of older USB A flash drives and peripherals I need for work. This little guy handles everything without any lag or connection drops. I've tried other adapters that get weirdly hot or disconnect randomly, but this one stays cool even during large file transfers. It's barely bigger than the port itself, so I just leave it plugged in all the time. Way better build quality than I anticipated for the price. Genuinely impressed.

I'd honestly only suggest this to someone running cable along a baseboard. The build quality is decent and the channel itself looks clean once you get everything snapped together, but the included adhesive is pretty hit or miss. Mine held up on a flat surface in the living room no problem, but the section I ran up the wall started peeling after about three weeks. Ended up using my own mounting strips and that solved it. Getting thicker gauge wire into the compartment was a tight squeeze but doable. For the price it's a fair deal if you're willing to swap out the tape. Just don't trust what comes in the box for vertical runs.

Arrived two days earlier than expected in a sturdy box with plenty of bubble wrap, so no worries about damage in transit. Unboxed it and the build feels solid for the price point. Took it out to the lake that same afternoon and snapped some photos near the water. Image clarity impressed me right away, especially for something this affordable. Buttons are intuitive enough that I didn't need the manual. Battery compartment sealed tight and everything felt secure. For a budget waterproof camera, this exceeded what I thought I'd get. Definitely recommend for casual outdoor adventures where you don't want to risk an expensive rig.

Picked this up to segment traffic between our office VoIP system and the rest of the network. Configuration was straightforward once I dug into the web interface, and VLAN tagging has been rock solid since day one. The build quality feels sturdy enough for a rack mount, and it runs surprisingly cool compared to my old Netgear. Knocked off one star because the initial firmware took a weirdly long time to load on first boot, and the documentation could definitely be clearer for someone not super familiar with managed switches. That said, for the price point, you really can't complain. Handling everything I've thrown at it without breaking a sweat.

Got this on sale and honestly couldn't be happier. The 1080p IPS screen is gorgeous for the money - colors pop and viewing angles are great for watching movies in bed. Boot time is instant like you'd expect from Chrome OS, and it handles dozens of Chrome tabs without breaking a sweat. Keyboard feels solid and the trackpad clicks are crisp across the whole surface. Battery easily gets me through a full workday plus evening browsing. Sure it's not a gaming machine, but for emails, docs, and streaming this checks every box. My kid uses it for schoolwork and I grab it for couch browsing. At this price point you really can't go wrong.

Honestly expected a lot more based on the hype around these. The connectivity is solid and pairing with my phone was instant, but the audio quality is pretty underwhelming for the price point. Music sounds flat, like there's no real depth to the bass at all. Calls are decent, nobody's complained about not hearing me, and the mic does a fine job blocking out background noise. Battery gets me through a workday with maybe 20 percent left, which is acceptable but not great. They're lightweight and comfortable enough for a few hours, but after that the ear pressure gets noticeable. For half the cost I'd say these are a decent pickup, but at full retail I'd look elsewhere. Not bad, just not impressive.

Got this for marathon training and it's been solid for the most part. The strap holds tight even on long sweaty runs, no bouncing or slipping at all which was my main concern. Sound quality is decent enough for podcasts and upbeat playlists. My one complaint is the navigation feels clunky, changing tracks mid-run takes some getting used to and I still fumble with it sometimes. Battery lasts through a week of daily runs before needing a charge. I'd recommend this to runners who want something affordable and reliable without needing fancy smartwatch features. If you're the type who likes scrolling through songs constantly during workouts though, maybe look elsewhere.

Got this for my home office setup and it's been fantastic. I use it to hold my iPad Pro at eye level next to my monitor for video calls and referencing documents while I work. The hinge mechanism is solid, no sagging or wobbling even when I'm tapping the screen constantly. Folds up nice and flat too, so I toss it in my bag when I travel for work. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who uses a tablet as a second screen or does a lot of video conferencing. Also great for following recipes in the kitchen or watching shows in bed. My mom liked mine so much she ordered one for her Kindle. Honestly can't beat it for the price.

I was hesitant to spend money on a grip but honestly this is worth every penny. The difference in handling is night and day with my E-M5. Before, my pinky would dangle off the bottom and shooting for hours left my hand cramping. Now the camera feels like a proper body and all the buttons are right where my fingers naturally rest. The shutter release on the grip itself has a really nice tactile feel too. Fit and finish is excellent with zero wobble once you lock it down. Getting the extra dial and function buttons at this price point is a steal compared to what other brands charge for their battery grips. If you're on the fence just buy it, you won't regret it.

Arrived in a padded envelope with zero bubble wrap or protection. The box was crushed on one corner and the plastic display window was cracked. I figured I'd try it anyway since the unit itself looked intact, but honestly it felt super cheap right out of the box. The buttons have this mushy feel and the screen had a small scratch already. Plugged it into my cigarette lighter and the connection was wobbly from the start. Sound came through with a constant hiss no matter what frequency I picked. Didn't even bother testing the aux cable. Packed it back up the same night and requested a refund. Don't waste your time, the build quality alone tells you everything you need to know.

I've had this center channel running for almost three years now in a pretty demanding setup, and it still performs like the day I unboxed it. My kids have bumped it, the dog has brushed against the grilles, and it's powered through countless movie marathons without a hiccup. The folded motion tweeter hasn't lost any crispness, and dialogue stays razor sharp even during chaotic action scenes. I paired it with some older bookshelf speakers from a different brand and it blends surprisingly well. Build quality is genuinely solid, heavy cabinet, quality binding posts, no rattles or buzzes after all this time. For the money, I don't think you can do better for a center. No regrets whatsoever.

Bought these for the gym and I'm genuinely impressed. The thing that sold me is the earhook design, they stay locked in no matter how much I'm moving. I've tried three other pairs that would pop out during running or bench press, but these don't budge. Battery gets me through about four workouts before needing a charge, and the case is small enough to forget in my pocket. Call quality is decent, not amazing, but music sounds full with punchy bass. Pairing was instant with my Pixel. For the price I honestly wasn't expecting this level of build. My buddy has AirPods Pro and these sound 90% as good for a fraction of the cost. Already recommended them to two people at my gym.

Box arrived a little beat up on one corner but the unit itself was fine inside. Took maybe twenty minutes to get everything hooked up in my Accord and the fit was clean enough. Boot up takes a few seconds longer than I expected but the screen looks sharp and responsive once it's running. Paired my phone without any issues and calls come through clear. Haven't tested navigation much yet but Google Maps loaded fine on first try. My one gripe so far is the included harness wires felt pretty thin and cheap compared to stock. For the price though it's a solid upgrade over the factory display. Gonna run it for a couple weeks before I decide if it's staying long term but first impressions are mostly positive.

Got this case about three weeks ago for my 10th gen iPad and overall I'm pretty happy with it. The fit is snug and all the cutouts line up perfectly with the speakers and charging port. I like that the front cover folds into a stand for typing or watching videos, though the angle could be a touch steeper for my liking when it's on a lower table. The material feels solid and has a nice grip so I'm not worried about it sliding around. My one minor gripe is the magnetic closure could be a bit stronger since it sometimes pops open in my bag if I'm not careful. Still, for the price it's a good buy and does what it needs to do without any real issues.

Bought this to digitize my family's old home movies on VHS and honestly it's been a frustrating ordeal from day one. The machine powers on fine but the recording quality is terrible. Every DVD I've burned has major skipping issues and audio sync problems about ten minutes in. The menu system is confusing and the remote feels cheap, like it might stop working any second. I tried three different brands of blank discs thinking that was the issue, but no luck. Called customer support twice and both times they just told me to reset the unit, which fixed nothing. I've wasted countless hours and a stack of discs on this thing. For the price, I expected way better. Going to cut my losses and look for something else.

Bought this for a home workbench setup after my cheaper dock gave out. Honestly, it does the job better than I expected for the price. Connection is solid and I haven't had any dropouts when cloning drives or running diagnostics. The top door is a bit loose though, it kind of just rests in place rather than clicking shut firmly. I learned that the hard way after tilting it and having the drive slide right out. As long as you keep it flat on your desk you're fine, but don't expect to use it at any weird angles. For what it is, a basic open-air test rig, it's decent value. Just wish the lid had a proper latch mechanism. Four stars because it works well despite that quirk.

I've had this running across my warehouse for about eight months now, connecting a label printer and barcode scanner to the front office computer. The cable is routed along the ceiling, zip-tied to beams, and has survived Forklifts brushing past it more times than I can count. No shielding issues, no kinks, the connectors still seat firmly on both ends. I was worried 50 feet might cause lag or dropouts but data transfer has been rock solid every single day. Even the jacket is holding up well despite temperature swings in the building. Honestly expected to replace this by now given the abuse it takes, but it just keeps working. Genuinely impressed with the build quality. Would buy again without hesitation.

Got this to mess around with off-camera flash outdoors and it does the job without breaking the bank. Used it on a couple portrait shoots now and the diffusion is pretty solid for what I need. Folds up nicely into the carry pouch, though getting it back in there took me a few attempts and a YouTube tutorial. The reflective surface is decently bright and seems to throw light back where I aim it. Build quality is okay, not amazing. You can tell it's a budget item. The frame feels a little flimsy if you're rough with it, so I'm pretty careful when setting up. Overall though, for the price I really can't complain. Gets the job done and hasn't let me down yet.

Got this to connect my wireless earbuds to my older stereo receiver so I could listen to music without waking everyone up. Setup was pretty painless and it paired without much fuss, which I appreciated. The dealbreaker for me is the audio lag. Watching videos is basically impossible because the lips don't match up with the sound at all. It's slightly less noticeable if you're just streaming music, but even then there's this faint constant hiss underneath everything that drives me crazy during quiet parts. Honestly, if you only need this for listening to podcasts or music where perfect sync doesn't matter, it's an okay budget option. But I can't recommend it for gaming or watching shows. Spend a little more and get something with aptX low latency support.

Picked this up for a fraction of what the big-name brands charge and honestly the image quality shocked me. Daytime footage is razor sharp and the night vision reaches way further down my driveway than I expected. Setup was painless, hooked it to my DVR, pulled up the on-screen menu, and had it dialed in within ten minutes. The weatherproofing is legit too. We've had two solid weeks of heavy rain and freezing temps and the thing hasn't skipped a beat. Mount feels solid and the adjustability once it's locked in is great. For what you're paying, you're getting performance that rivals cameras costing three times as much. Already ordered a second one to cover the side yard. Can't ask for more than that.

Total waste of money. I bought this thinking the extra channels would help with my Xfinity 100 Mbps plan, but my speeds actually dropped compared to the cheap Motorola I'd been renting for years. Best case I'm seeing 40 down on a good day, and half the time pages just hang while the modem randomly reboots itself. Called my ISP twice and they confirmed the signal levels are fine, so it's definitely this thing. For what I paid, I expected at least comparable performance to a basic model, not worse speeds and constant drops. Going back to my old setup until I find something that actually works. Don't be fooled by the channel count on paper, it means nothing if the hardware can't deliver.

I needed a simple GPS for my mom who is terrible with technology and this fit the bill perfectly. No confusing menus, no unnecessary features she will never use. Just enter an address and go. I have a high-end Garmin that cost triple and honestly this little thing gets me to the same destination just fine. It locks onto satellites within about ten seconds of turning it on and the voice prompts are clear enough to hear over the radio. The mount is basic but holds steady on the windshield. This is not the unit for someone wanting traffic updates or Bluetooth calling. But for an older parent, a teen driver, or anyone wanting straightforward navigation without the learning curve, this is the one. Can't beat it for the price.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this little thing packs a serious punch. I've been using it on my patio for a few weeks now and it fills the whole backyard without distortion. The battery lasts way longer than I anticipated, I only charge it maybe once a week with regular use. My brother has a JBL that cost four times as much and yeah, his sounds a bit richer, but not four-hundred-percent better. The pairing is instant every time I turn it on, no fiddling around. Dropped it on concrete once and not a scratch or hiccup. If you're on the fence, just get it. For what this costs, it way overdelivers. Would happily buy again.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price, figured it'd be a minor step up from my old HTIB center channel. Boy was I wrong. Dialog clarity jumped massively, no more cranking the volume during quiet scenes then getting blasted when action kicks in. Voices have real weight to them instead of that tinny, boxed-in sound I'd just accepted as normal. I was nervous because my room is pretty open and I figured a budget center wouldn't keep up, but it fills the space without straining. Compared to the Polk it replaced (which cost me double), this thing is honestly clearer and less muddy in the midrange. Only complaint is it's heavier than expected and I had to reinforce my shelf. For the money, way beyond what I anticipated.

Got these for work since I kept destroying my expensive earbuds at the warehouse. Figured for eight bucks I'd give them a shot and honestly I'm impressed. The sound is surprisingly full - not amazing by any stretch but way better than the gas station ones I used to buy. They block out my coworker's radio pretty well which is all I needed. The cord feels a bit thin and I'm sure it'll eventually short out near the jack like every cheap pair does, but at this price I'll just order another set. The inline mic works fine for quick calls though people say I sound slightly muffled. Overall you genuinely can't beat these for the money. Not premium but absolutely gets the job done.

Wasn't sure what to expect from a budget fan controller but this little unit really delivered. My previous one was a cheap no-name thing that died after six months and made everything rattle. This one feels way more solid and the knobs actually have some resistance to them instead of turning loosely like cheap junk. Slides right into a 5.25 bay no problem, wiring was straightforward even for someone like me who hates cable management. Running four 120mm fans off it and the difference is night and day. Full speed when gaming, dial them down to basically silent for regular browsing. Honestly expected to be returning this based on the price but it's been running solid for about two months now with zero issues. Way better quality than I anticipated.

Honestly expected more from these. The concept is great but the execution falls flat. The material has a memory effect where it keeps springing back into a coiled shape no matter what you do. I tried stretching them out, laying them flat under weights for a day, nothing worked. They just bunch up and look messy on the desk. The connectors also feel cheap and don't seat properly in my devices, like there's a slight mismatch in the sizing. Every time I bump the cable slightly it loses connection. For the price I paid these should at least function reliably. Spent the extra money on a name brand set instead and wish I'd done that from the start. Skip these.

Picked this up for my laptop about two years ago and I have mixed feelings. On the plus side, the compact size is perfect for tossing in my bag and the build quality is surprisingly solid for the price. The scroll wheel is genuinely nice and tactile. But the battery drain is frustrating, I'm swapping AA batteries every five or six weeks with moderate use, which adds up. Around the eighteen-month mark the left click started acting up, sometimes registering double clicks when I only pressed once. It still works if I'm careful, but it gets annoying during long work sessions. For casual use it's decent value, but if you're on your computer all day you'll probably want something more reliable.

Switched out my old rented router for this TP-Link model and honestly wish I had done it months ago. The whole process took maybe ten minutes from opening the box to having every device back online. I just powered down my Spectrum modem, hooked up the new router, and waited for the lights to stabilize. My iPhone, two smart TVs, and my desktop all reconnected without any hiccups. The signal reaches every corner of my two-story house, even the back bedroom where I used to get dead spots. Speeds are noticeably faster than what I was getting before, and I've had zero dropouts in the week since I installed it. Solid build quality too. Definitely recommend if you're tired of paying your ISP every month for outdated equipment.

Bought this mainly so I could check the outdoor temp from my kitchen, and honestly it's been pretty disappointing. The signal drops constantly if there's more than one wall between the sensor and the display unit. My old AcuRite handled the same spot without any issues for years, so I figured this would be comparable. Nope. I have to walk toward the back door just to get a reading to update, which kind of defeats the whole point. The indoor temp seems accurate enough, and the display itself looks fine on the counter. But if you're expecting reliable outdoor monitoring from any real distance, you'll be frustrated. Considering what I paid, I expected better range. Two stars because at least it turns on and gives a number sometimes.

Picked these up on sale for around $30 and honestly, for that price, I'm pretty satisfied. The build quality is solid, aluminum shells that don't feel cheap, and the detachable cable is a nice touch you don't usually see at this tier. Sound-wise, they definitely lean warm and bass-forward, which works great for hip-hop and electronic stuff. Vocals can get a bit recessed and the treble isn't the most detailed, but nothing a little EQ can't fix. Comfort is decent for long sessions, though the nozzles are on the wider side. Included tips are just okay, I swapped to SpinFits and got a much better seal. Not a perfect IEM by any means, but the accessories and overall presentation make these a solid budget pick.

Picked this up hoping for a compact Bluetooth mouse to pair with my travel laptop, and it's honestly just okay. The size is right, slips into my sleeve pocket without adding bulk, and the Bluetooth connection holds up decently well. But I expected smoother tracking based on the listing. On darker surfaces it stutters noticeably, which defeats the purpose of a travel mouse since you never know what desk or table you'll end up on. The click feel is fine, maybe a little loud for meetings. Battery life has been acceptable so far, nothing remarkable. It does the job if your expectations are modest, but I've used better mice in this price range. Not mad I bought it, just not wowed either. Probably wouldn't grab it again.

Ordered this online and it showed up in a padded envelope that was practically shredded. The corner of the case was poking through the packaging and already had a scuff on it right out of the mail. Not a great start. I figured I'd give it a shot anyway since the damage was just cosmetic. Slid my iPad in and the fit is honestly mediocre. The right side clips grab okay but the left side feels loose and doesn't inspire much confidence. The material itself is decent and slim, I'll give it that, but I can already tell those clips are going to be a problem. For the price I expected better quality control and at minimum packaging that actually protects the product. Looking into returning it.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this thing completely blew me away. I needed something to bridge a wired hotel connection to my phone and laptop during a work trip, and figured I'd be stuck with some clunky setup process. Nope, plugged it in, followed a couple quick steps, and was online in under five minutes. The signal strength is way better than I anticipated for something this small. I was getting full bars across a decent-sized hotel room. Even handled my video calls without dropping. My only minor gripe is there's no included pouch, so I just tossed it in a spare sunglasses bag. For what it costs, you really can't complain. Way exceeded what I thought I was getting.

Honestly didn't expect much for the price but this little adapter has been holding its own on my 2014 Mac mini for about six months now. I needed something to run two extra monitors for work and this does the job without too much fuss. There's an occasional screen flicker when the machine wakes from sleep, which is annoying but not a dealbreaker. Just unplug and replug and you're back in business. Build quality is better than I anticipated, doesn't feel like it'll snap in half if you look at it wrong. The included cable is a bit short though, so plan accordingly if your setup has any distance between ports. Works way better than the no-name one I tried first from a local electronics shop. Decent buy overall.

Picked this up a few months back and I have mixed feelings. The video quality is decent for casual stuff, family gatherings, quick clips on vacation, and it's genuinely pocket-sized, which I love. But the fixed storage drives me crazy. If you're out shooting all day, you're stuck deleting footage to make room, and there's no swapping in a card. Battery life is just okay, maybe 45 minutes of continuous recording before it dies. You also can't pop in a spare battery, so you're tethered to a wall outlet. I'd recommend this to someone who just wants a simple, grab-and-go cam for short clips and doesn't care about expandability. If you need something for longer shoots, look elsewhere.

Bought this dock for my XPS 15 thinking I'd get a clean dual monitor setup with one cable. What a joke. The ethernet port drops connection every 20 minutes like clockwork. I'll be in the middle of a Zoom call and suddenly everyone freezes. The only fix is to unplug and replug the whole dock, which also kills my displays for about 30 seconds while everything reconnects. I tried updating firmware and drivers but the Dell updater doesn't even recognize the dock is connected half the time. The USB ports work fine for my keyboard and mouse, so I guess that's something, but I didn't spend this much for a glorified USB hub. Going back to my old reliable Anker dock that actually stays connected. Save your money.

I shoot a lot of outdoor macro photography and needed a tripod that could handle uneven terrain without toppling over. This thing has been fantastic for that. The legs lock into basically any angle you want, so I can get my camera low to the ground for flower shots or set it up on a rocky hillside without worrying about stability. Build quality feels solid, nothing flimsy or cheap about it. The quick-release plate works smoothly and holds my DSLR with a heavy lens attached without any wobble. I'd definitely recommend this to nature photographers, vloggers who shoot on location, or really anyone tired of flimsy tripods that can't handle awkward setups. For the price, you're getting way more than you'd expect. Gonna be using this for years.

Been using this for about three weeks now and honestly I'm kicking myself for waiting so long to buy one. Setup took maybe ten minutes start to finish, and the image quality is way sharper than I thought it would be for the price. I've tried a couple similar products before and always ended up returning them, but this one actually delivers on what it claims. The controls make sense without having to dig through confusing submenus every time you want to change something. Build quality feels solid too, not cheap or flimsy like some of the competitors. Only minor gripe is the included paperwork is pretty bare bones, but honestly you don't really need it. Already recommended it to two coworkers who are placing orders. Great purchase all around.

For the price, I honestly wasn't expecting premium materials, so I'm not too upset. The faux leather exterior looks decent enough from a distance and the overall fit on the tablet is nice and snug. It does the basic job of protecting my device from scratches and minor bumps. That said, the magnetic clasp is already getting weak after about six weeks of daily use. It shuts off the screen fine when closed, but the flap doesn't always stay secured if I toss it in my bag. The edges also started peeling a bit near the spine. It's an okay budget option if you just need something cheap, but manage your expectations on durability. You get what you pay for here.

Paid almost $900 for this and it's honestly the worst purchase I've made in years. You'd expect decent quality at this price point but the screen started getting dead pixels after just four months. The smart features are a joke too, apps crash constantly and the whole interface lags like crazy. My old $300 budget TV worked better than this. Called customer support and they want me to ship it back at my own expense for repair, which would take weeks. Are you kidding me? For what I paid, this should last longer than a season. The picture quality when it actually works is fine I guess, but nothing that justifies the premium price tag. Save your money and buy literally anything else. Total ripoff.

Honestly, I had higher hopes for this cover based on the listing. The fit is snug and all the cutouts line up properly with my charging port and speakers, which I appreciate. But the material feels a lot thinner in person than it looks in the photos. After about six weeks of daily use, I'm already noticing the edges around the fold are getting worn and slightly fuzzy. It does the job if you just want basic scratch protection for tossing it in a bag, but I wouldn't call it heavy-duty by any stretch. The magnetic closure works fine, nothing fancy. For the price I guess it's acceptable, but I was expecting something a bit more substantial. Probably fine for light use, just don't expect premium build quality.

Picked these up on a whim because the retro-futuristic design caught my eye and the price seemed reasonable enough to take a chance. Honestly, for what they cost, I wasn't expecting audiophile quality, and these definitely aren't that. The sound is muddy in the lower end and the highs have a tinny edge to them. That said, they're serviceable if you just want something for casual background listening. My real issue is the build. The plastic feels cheap and creaky, and the ear cushions press hard against my ears. After about forty minutes they get genuinely painful. The headband adjustment is loose too and keeps slipping. They look neat sitting on a shelf, but as actual daily-use headphones the value just isn't there.

I've been using this diffuser on my speedlight for about eight months now, shooting mostly indoor portraits and events. It's held up way better than I expected. The plastic hasn't yellowed or cracked, and the fit is still snug on my flash head without any wobble. I've tossed it in my camera bag loose among lenses and bodies, and it's picked up zero scratches or dents. Light output is soft and even, really knocks down those harsh shadows you get from bouncing off low ceilings. What surprised me most is how well the mounting tab has stayed springy after hundreds of attach/detach cycles. Cheaper ones I've tried got loose within a month. This one feels like it'll outlast the flash itself. Grab one, you won't regret it.

Been using these daily for about four months now and they're still going strong. I'm rough on earbuds, stuff them in pockets, yank the cord, leave them in a hot car, and these have held up way better than pairs I've paid triple for. The wire hasn't frayed near the jack like most do, and the rubber tips stay on secure. Sound is solid for the money, nothing mind-blowing but way above what I expected. Bass is punchy enough for podcasts and casual music. The mic works fine for calls, maybe slightly muffled on my end according to coworkers but totally usable. Volume slider is a nice touch. Only complaint is the fit gets a little uncomfortable after a couple hours. For what they cost, honestly can't complain. Would buy again.

Worked okay for the first three months on my X58 board, gave me the extra SATA ports I needed for a RAID setup. But last week one of the port connectors literally came loose inside the cable when I went to swap a drive out. The plastic feels super flimsy and the solder points on the board are weak. Now two of the four ports are dead completely. For something that sits inside a case and shouldn't get bumped, there's no excuse for it falling apart this fast. The chipset runs hot too, noticed the heatsink was loose when I first installed it but didn't think much of it. Spend a little more and get something built to last.

Bought this adapter for a penetration testing course and it honestly exceeded all my expectations. The range is incredible, I was picking up networks my laptop's built-in card couldn't even see. Packet injection worked flawlessly right out of the box on Kali Linux with zero driver headaches, which is rare for these types of adapters. The build quality feels solid enough for regular travel use, and the included antenna does a respectable job. I've spent weeks running various security audits around my home lab and it hasn't dropped connection once. For anyone doing wireless security work or just needing a serious long-range Wi-Fi adapter, this is the one to get. Easily worth double what they're charging. Will definitely buy another for my travel kit.

Bought this for my daily commute after my old player died. Build quality is decent and the interface is straightforward enough once you get the hang of it. Battery gets me through most of the work week on a single charge, which I appreciate. Where it falls short is the audio. Coming from older Sony models, the output feels thinner and less warm than I expected. It's not bad, just underwhelming for the price tag. I'd recommend this to someone who wants a simple, reliable music player for the gym or casual listening and doesn't care about audiophile-level sound. If you're picky about audio depth, you might want to look elsewhere or invest in better headphones to compensate. Three stars because it does the job, just nothing special.

I've been towing a 28ft travel trailer for years and always struggled with blind spots when reversing.
