The movie itself is pretty forgettable honestly, Mira Sorvino tries but the romance feels forced and the pacing drags. Expected better longevity from a retail copy. Glad I didn't pay full price for this one.

Watched this over a weekend and really enjoyed the contrasting perspectives on where technology is heading. The futurist segments are fascinating but I especially appreciated the ethicist interviews who pushed back on the hype. My only gripe is the middle episode drags a bit and repeats points already made. Still, it sparked a great conversation with my wife afterward. Worth your time if you're into tech philosophy.

I've had this DVD set for about three years now and it still plays flawlessly. My kids have handled the discs more times than I can count and there's not a single scratch or skip. The cases have held up great too, no cracked hinges. Dench is absolutely brilliant in this role. If you want a show the whole family can enjoy that actually holds up physically, grab it.

Got this for under ten bucks and it's worth every penny. Chris keeps things moving without being annoying, and the combo segments actually make the time fly by. I've done this routine maybe fifteen times now and still don't get bored. The catch drill is goofy fun but genuinely gets your heart rate going. Solid full-body workout that I'll keep reaching for.

Picked this up on sale and honestly can't believe how much content you get for the money. Six films, all remastered beautifully, plus a ton of behind-the-scenes extras that actually add something. The transfer on the first movie alone is worth what I paid. Packaging feels sturdy too, not some flimsy cardboard thing. If you've been holding off, just go for it. You won't find a better deal on a collection this solid anywhere.

The case arrived with a cracked corner, which was disappointing. Shipping took longer than expected too. As for the movie itself, it starts pretty rough and took me a couple sittings to get through. Eventually it picks up and finishes strong, but man, that opening act is a slog. Not terrible overall, just not something I'd rush to revisit. Glad I watched it once at least.

Really enjoyed this deep dive into Welles' career and personality. The archival clips are fantastic and give you a real sense of why he was so magnetic on screen. My only gripe is it breezes past some of his later projects without much detail. Still, as someone who only knew the basics going in, I came away with a much fuller picture of the man. Definitely worth a watch if you're into film history.

I've had this DVD set for over three years now and it still plays perfectly despite being lent out to friends countless times. The discs hold up amazingly well with no scratching issues. The episodes themselves are pure gold, the cast finally hits their stride and every sketch lands. Watched it probably fifteen times and it never gets old. Totally worth every penny.

I've watched this Blu-ray probably a dozen times over the past two years and it still plays perfectly. No scratches, no skipping, even though I've lent it to three different friends. The transfer holds up well on my 4K setup too. The film itself is a solid survival epic with great performances. My only minor gripe is the extras are pretty thin. But for the price, this disc has been incredibly durable and totally worth picking up.

Honestly expected another generic animated love story but this completely caught me off guard. The humor actually lands instead of relying on tired slapstick, and the leads feel like real people you'd run into. I figured my kids would enjoy it and I'd just be sitting through it, but I laughed harder than they did at multiple scenes. Watched it twice already this week. Disney really stepped outside their usual formula here and nailed it.

Watched this with my wife on a whim and we both sat in silence when the credits rolled. That rarely happens. The way the story handles guilt and redemption without being preachy is something else entirely. I've never seen a film capture the weight of a single mistake so authentically. We ended up talking about it for days after. Already ordered a second copy for my brother. Just an unforgettable piece of filmmaking.

Had this disc sitting in my collection for about three years now and it still plays flawlessly despite being lent out to coworkers multiple times. The case hasn't cracked and the disc surface holds up well even with my less-than-careful handling. Picture quality blows away the streaming version I tried first. The movie itself gets better every rewatch as you catch little details you missed. Glad I grabbed the physical copy instead of going digital.

Bought this after a coworker wouldn't stop raving about it, and honestly it exceeded my expectations. The chapter on WWII and the atomic bombings alone is worth the price. Stone digs into declassified documents you never see in standard textbooks, and the archival footage quality is surprisingly sharp for the era. My only gripe is the soundtrack gets repetitive by episode six. Still, this completely changed how I view Cold War foreign policy. Highly recommend for anyone who questions the mainstream narrative.

Ordered the Blu-ray for movie night and it arrived two days early in a sturdy mailer with no cracks on the case. The slipcover looked sharp with minimal shelf wear. Popped it in right away and the picture quality blew me away on my living room setup. The DTS audio really kicks during the battle scenes. Only knock is the special features felt a little thin compared to what I expected. Still totally worth picking up though.

Finally sat down to watch this after years of hearing about it, and it completely lived up to the hype. The pacing is tight, the dialogue is razor-sharp, and the performances across the board are stellar. What surprised me most was how relevant the themes still feel decades later. The whole thing pulls you in from the opening scene and doesn't let go. A genuinely gripping watch from start to finish that absolutely deserves its reputation.

Got this about four months ago and watched it maybe a dozen times. The disc itself plays fine, no skipping issues at all. My main gripe is how flimsy the case feels. The hinge on one side already snapped, and the center hub doesn't grip the disc like it should. I have to be super careful opening it or the disc slides right out. Movie's great and the transfer looks solid, but the packaging really leaves something to be desired for the price.

Saw this back when it came out and just rewatched it on streaming. Holds up incredibly well. The surveillance stuff is even more relevant now than it was then. Will Smith plays the wrong guy perfectly and Hackman is great as the paranoid ex-intel guy living off the grid. If you have friends who think privacy is a thing of the past, show them this. Perfect double feature with The Net for a 90s paranoia night.

Ordered this Blu-ray on a Tuesday and it showed up by Friday in a padded mailer with no damage to the case at all. Popped it in right away and the transfer looks way better than I expected for a movie this old. Sound was crisp too. Only watched the first half hour so far but already laughing out loud. Glad I finally picked this up instead of just streaming it. Solid purchase all around.

Arrived two days earlier than expected in a sturdy mailer with zero corner dents, which I always appreciate for DVD collecting. The case artwork looks sharp and the disc was seated properly with no scratches. Popped it in right away and the menu loaded fast with clean subtitle options. Picture quality on my setup looked great right from the opening scene. Really impressed with the overall presentation and packaging. Can't wait to sit down and watch the whole thing this weekend.

I've had this DVD in my collection for about three years now and it still plays perfectly despite being lent out to friends multiple times. The disc itself is surprisingly durable with no scratches or skipping issues. Widmark is absolutely chilling as the villain, and Mature brings real weight to his role as the ex-con trying to take down the mob. That infamous staircase scene still gives me chills every watch. A classic noir that holds up beautifully after countless viewings.

I expected this to be just another generic action flick but it genuinely surprised me. The pacing is tight, the tone is perfectly gritty, and the lead absolutely owns every scene he's in. I figured the story would be predictable but there are enough twists to keep things interesting all the way through. Way better than most of the stuff coming out today. If you want a solid crime thriller that actually delivers, this is worth picking up. Glad I grabbed it.

I bought this on a whim after my coworker wouldn't shut up about it. Man, was he right. Following Easy Company from training all the way through Europe puts you right there with those guys in a way no documentary ever has. The interviews with the actual veterans hit incredibly hard. I'd recommend this to anyone who thinks they don't like war stories. My wife binged the whole thing in a weekend. Gifting it to my dad for his birthday.

The DVD arrived in one of those flimsy mailers with zero bubble wrap, so naturally the case was cracked right down the middle. Disc played fine at least. The movie itself is pretty forgettable low-budget stuff from the late sixties. Dull pacing, cheesy effects, and the print quality looks like nobody bothered cleaning it up. Not the worst thing I've sat through but definitely not worth a rewatch. Two stars for getting here on time, minus three for the lousy packaging and mediocre transfer.

The pacing threw me off at first since the opening feels pretty generic and predictable. Almost turned it off but glad I stuck around. The second half really shifts gears and the camera work gets noticeably more polished. The acting from the younger cast members is what sold me though, they carry the emotional scenes surprisingly well. Not perfect by any means and some plot points feel rushed, but overall a solid family watch that exceeded my expectations.

I've been collecting these season sets and season thirteen is honestly one of my favorites. The cast chemistry really clicks here, and Fred Thompson slides into the DA role perfectly. The 300th episode is a great milestone that fans will appreciate. Gregory Hines puts in a memorable guest appearance too. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who followed the show during its original run or newcomers who enjoy procedural dramas. The cases feel fresh and the writing stays sharp throughout. Solid addition to any collection.

Vince Vaughn basically plays Vince Vaughn again here, which is fine if you're into that fast-talking thing he does. The scenery is genuinely gorgeous and probably the real standout. I watched the Blu-ray and the transfer makes those landscapes pop beautifully, so points for that. The comedy itself is pretty hit or miss though. I chuckled a couple times but mostly sat through predictable jokes. Not a terrible way to kill an evening, just don't expect anything fresh.

I went in with zero expectations and was genuinely surprised by how tense this gets. The sound design is what really sold it for me, every creak and whisper through the surround speakers had me looking over my shoulder. Yeah the plot gets a little messy in the third act and some of the CGI hasn't aged gracefully, but the atmosphere never lets up. Watch it alone with the lights off and decent speakers and you'll have a good time. Not a masterpiece but absolutely worth a Friday night rental.

My rheumatologist suggested I try gentle yoga at home between physical therapy appointments, and this has been a game changer. The pace is perfect for someone dealing with chronic pain and stiffness. What I really appreciate is how the instructor never pushes you beyond what your body can handle that day. Some mornings I can only do fifteen minutes, and that's totally fine. The movements closely mirror what my PT had me doing in the clinic. Really glad I found this one.

I'll give it two stars because the world-building is genuinely incredible. The alien cityscapes and creature designs are some of the best I've seen in years, and I kept pausing just to take in the background details. But man, the script is a complete mess. The lead character has zero personality and makes baffling decisions every five minutes. By the halfway point I honestly didn't care what happened to anyone. It's frustrating because there's a brilliant movie buried in here somewhere beneath all the confusing dialogue and pointless subplots. Watch it on mute maybe.

I'll admit the action sequences are top notch and Craig brings a grittier edge that I appreciated. What bugged me though was the pacing. The middle act drags badly with long exposition scenes that killed the momentum for me. By the time the third act ramped up again I'd kinda lost interest. Judi Dench is great as always and the cinematography looks fantastic on blu ray. Just wish they'd trimmed about twenty minutes out of the middle and tightened things up. Decent Bond film but not one I'll revisit often.

Ordered this on Blu-ray and it arrived two days earlier than expected. The case was in one of those sturdy cardboard mailers with air pillows, so no cracks or bent corners. Popped it in right away and the transfer looks way better than I remember on old cable reruns. Solid picture quality and the sound is decent too. Really fun crime caper with a great ensemble. Took off one star because the special features are pretty thin. Still a solid pickup for the price.

Watched this with a group of friends last weekend and we were all hooked within the first twenty minutes. The claustrophobic setting really works in its favor, and the dread builds gradually instead of relying on cheap jump scares. A few plot points left us scratching our heads and wishing for more backstory, but honestly the atmosphere was strong enough that it didn't ruin the experience. The pacing keeps things moving and the tension between characters feels genuine. Solid pick for a horror night when you want something that actually gets under your skin.

Watched this with my kids last weekend and we had an absolute blast. The action kicks off right away and barely lets up for two hours. Fraser is hilarious as O'Connell, and Weisz balances the comedy with real charm. Some of the CGI hasn't aged perfectly, but honestly it adds to the fun. The finale in the jungle is visually stunning and had everyone cheering. Perfect popcorn movie for family movie night. Already planning to rewatch it next month.

Stumbled onto this late at night and ended up watching the whole thing in one sitting. The premise feels terrifyingly plausible, not some far-fetched sci-fi fantasy but something that genuinely could unfold the way technology is heading. What impressed me most was how much tension they built without relying on big effects or recognizable faces. The two leads carry the story convincingly and the dialogue never felt forced. For a smaller production, the pacing is tight and the ending stuck with me for days. Genuinely wish more people knew about this one.

My buddy told me this was the scariest thing he'd watched all year, so I went in with high expectations. Honestly? It's fine if you're a teenager at a sleepover who hasn't seen many horror films and just wants something playing in the background. The atmosphere works in a couple of scenes, but the pacing drags and the ending left me frustrated. If you're a seasoned horror fan looking for genuine scares or original ideas, skip it. I'd only recommend this to casual viewers who scare easily.

I read the book first and absolutely loved it, so maybe my expectations were too high. The movie version of The Help just doesn't capture what makes the novel so powerful. So much gets glossed over or compressed that the emotional weight disappears. The relationships between the maids and their employers feel surface-level compared to what Kathryn Stockett wrote. Viola Davis is great, but even she can't save a script that rushes through major plot points. It's an okay watch if you haven't read the book, but honestly you're better off skipping this and reading instead.

I picked this up on a whim and ended up bingeing the whole thing over a weekend. The locations are filmed really well and you get a solid sense of scale with each site. Some of the narration made me raise an eyebrow, a few dates and details felt off, so I wouldn't use this as a textbook replacement. That said, it's a great jumping-off point if you're curious about ancient cultures but don't want to sit through a dense lecture. I'd happily recommend it to casual history fans and older kids who are just starting to explore the subject.

Honestly wasn't sure how they'd balance so many main characters but Whedon nailed it. Every hero gets their moment to shine without it feeling overcrowded. The banter between Tony Stark and Steve Rogers alone is worth the price. Action sequences are top-notch and the final battle in New York still gives me chills. My kids and I have probably watched this fifteen times and nobody reaches for their phone. If you somehow haven't seen it yet, fix that immediately. Great popcorn flick.

My dad served in the Pacific theater, so I grew up hearing WWII stories my whole life. Most war shows feel Hollywood-glamorized, but what sold me on this series was how raw the combat scenes feel. The Bastogne episodes especially, the cold, the confusion, the sheer terror of being pinned down in those woods, it's almost too real. You genuinely care about every soldier because the character development happens gradually across all ten episodes. Watched the whole thing over a weekend and immediately started over with the cast commentary tracks.

I had high hopes for this Bond installment, but it really falls flat. Connery looks bored the whole time, and the plot feels like three scripts mashed together with no coherent direction. Max von Sydow is wasted in a role that could've been great. That said, I'd actually recommend this to Bond completionists or anyone doing a retro spy movie marathon. It's fun in a so-bad-it's-entertaining way if you go in with low expectations. Basinger tries her best and there are a couple decent action sequences. Just don't expect Thunderball-level quality. Two stars for nostalgia value alone.

Watched this with my wife over the weekend and we both really enjoyed it. The cast is absolutely stacked and everyone brings their A-game. Bale is barely recognizable and totally sells the role. The pacing drags a bit in the middle and some of the subplots feel unnecessary, but the last act pulls everything together nicely. The 70s aesthetic is spot on, from the wardrobes to the soundtrack. Not a perfect film by any means but definitely worth your time if you like character-driven crime dramas. Four solid stars from me.

Grabbed this on a whim and honestly wasn't expecting much. Boy was I wrong. The storyline grabbed me right from the opening scene and never really let go. What surprised me most was how polished everything felt considering the budget. The acting is solid across the board, and the pacing keeps things moving without any slow spots. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys offbeat thrillers that don't follow the usual Hollywood formula. If you're tired of the same recycled plots and want something that actually takes chances, this is worth your time and money. Watched it twice already.

Honestly, I expected this final season to be a letdown based on all the controversy online, but it really held up for me. Sure, the pacing isn't as tight as the earlier years and some storylines feel like they needed more room to breathe. Tony's downward spiral is genuinely uncomfortable to watch, which I think was the whole point. The supporting cast delivers some of their best work here, even if a few new characters don't get enough development. Not my favorite season, but a fitting end to an incredible series. Glad I finally added it to my collection.

Ordered this for a nostalgia binge and it arrived two days earlier than expected. The case was in perfect shape with no cracks, which is honestly rare for DVD sets shipped in bubble mailers. All three discs were secure in their slots and played without any skipping. Picture quality looks solid for a show from the early 70s and the menus load fast. My kids had never seen it and were hooked within the first episode. The Hawaii trip episodes alone make this season worth picking up. Really happy with this purchase overall and planning to grab season five next.

I'd recommend this to anyone who lived through the late 70s and early 80s comedy scene, or really anyone curious about performance art in general. Carrey nails Kaufman's mannerisms so perfectly that several scenes gave me chills. The pacing drags a bit in the middle and some of the Taxi Woman bits run too long, but that feels intentional given who this was about. My brother didn't get it at all and walked out bored. It's not a light watch, but if you appreciate boundary-pushing comedy and want to understand what made Kaufman so polarizing, give it a shot.

I'd been hunting for this on streaming for ages and finally grabbed the Blu-ray. If you're a fan of sweeping 1950s epics, this is a must-watch. The production values are honestly jaw-dropping for the era, those ocean sequences still hold up beautifully on a modern TV. I bought it for my parents who remembered seeing it on late-night TV decades ago, but I ended up watching it twice myself over the weekend. The performances are grounded and heartfelt, never overwrought. Perfect pick for classic film buffs or anyone wanting to share something special with older relatives. Glad I added this to my collection.

I've had this blu-ray for about eight months now and it's held up perfectly through multiple rewatches. The disc still loads fast and plays smooth with zero scratches or issues despite being handled pretty carelessly by my kids. The packaging is solid too, the case hasn't cracked and the cover art looks as good as the day I got it. The film itself is a chilling look at Uday Hussein's brutality through the eyes of his body double. Dominic Cooper absolutely kills it playing both roles. The transfer quality is sharp and the sound mix is incredible on a decent system. Definitely worth adding to your collection, holds up great over time.

I've owned this on DVD for going on six years now and it still gets regular play during Lent and Advent. The disc has held up beautifully after dozens of viewings, no freezing or degradation whatsoever. The transfer holds its quality even on my newer 4K setup, which surprised me. What keeps me coming back is how the soundtrack complements the storytelling without overwhelming it. The cinematography still looks gorgeous after all this time. My kids have watched it every Easter since they were little and now they ask for it by name. That says something about its staying power. If you want a Jesus film that holds up both physically and artistically, this is the one to get.

I honestly didn't expect much going into this. Figured it'd just be a dumb puppet movie with a few cheap laughs. Man, was I wrong. The puppet action sequences are actually shot really well, and the satire hits way harder than I anticipated. Some of the musical numbers had me literally crying laughing. I've seen plenty of comedies that don't come close to this level of commitment to the bit. The attention to detail in those miniature sets is impressive too. Yes, it's crude and over the top, but that's the whole point. If you're on the fence because you think it's just going to be low-effort shock humor, give it a shot. Way smarter and funnier than it has any right to be.

Got this complete box set on sale and honestly it's worth every penny. I looked at buying the seasons individually before and the cost added up fast. Getting everything in one package saved me a ton. The picture quality holds up well and each disc worked perfectly with no issues. My family has been marathoning episodes every weekend and we're already talking about rewatching from the beginning. The extra features were a nice surprise too, some good behind the scenes stuff. If you enjoyed this show when it aired, grab the whole set. Way cheaper than streaming subscriptions and you actually own it permanently.

Ordered this for my kids movie night and it arrived two days earlier than expected. The case came in a sturdy mailer with no cracks or bent corners, which honestly doesn't always happen with media orders online. Popped it in right after dinner and the whole family was glued to the screen. My seven year old had never seen a Peanuts film before and she was captivated from the opening notes. The animation holds up beautifully and the story has so much more emotional depth than I remembered from watching it as a kid. Picture quality is solid for a classic and the sound came through great on our living room setup. Really happy with this purchase overall.

I've had this import set sitting on my shelf for about three years now and it still plays flawlessly. The discs have survived multiple binge sessions and being loaned out to friends without any scratching or playback issues. Menu navigation is smooth and the video quality holds up great on my newer blu-ray player. Subtitles are clean and readable throughout both parts of the series. Packaging is sturdy too, the case hasn't cracked or gotten dinged despite moving twice since I bought it. Really glad I picked this up when I did since tracking down the original domestic releases is basically impossible without spending a fortune. If you're a fan of classic 90s fantasy comedy anime, this collection is worth every penny and then some.

I've had this blu-ray for about eight months now and it's held up great. My kids have gotten their hands on it more times than I can count, left it out of the case twice, and somehow it still plays without a single skip or glitch. The disc itself seems way more durable than most of the ones I buy. As for the actual movie, it took me a second viewing to really appreciate what they were going for. The pacing threw me off initially but once I stopped expecting a neat resolution it clicked. The performances feel genuine and the story lingers with you days after watching. Knocking off one star because the bonus features are pretty thin. Solid purchase overall though.

Went in expecting a lot more based on all the hype from horror fans. The concept of a med student turning to underground body modification is genuinely fresh, and Katharine Isabelle does a solid job in the lead. But the execution feels rushed and messy. Characters make bizarre decisions that pulled me right out of it, and the ending comes so abruptly I actually checked if my disc skipped. The surgery scenes look great and there's a slick visual style throughout, but the script needed another draft or two to tie everything together. Overall it's an okay watch for genre fans who want something different, just don't go in anticipating the masterpiece some people make it out to be.

Bought this for my niece's birthday and honestly it was a mixed bag. The kids were excited at first and actually did follow along with the choreography for maybe three or four days before losing interest completely. The production quality is decent enough but some of the song choices felt a little off for the target age group. A few of the moves made me side-eye the TV wondering who thought that was appropriate for seven-year-olds, though I'll admit the kids themselves had zero clue and were just bouncing around having fun. For the price it kept them occupied for a rainy weekend so I can't complain too much. Just wish there was a way to stream a sample before committing.

I'd heard so much hype about this one over the years that I honestly expected it to blow me away. It didn't quite reach that level for me, but I still really enjoyed it. The pacing drags a little in the second act and some of the jokes feel a bit dated, but the performances carry it through. The lead is genuinely charming and a few scenes caught me off guard with how funny they were. I was worried it wouldn't hold up after all these years, but mostly it does. Not a movie I'd rush to rewatch every holiday season, but definitely worth having in the collection. Glad I finally crossed it off the list.

Ordered the Blu-ray for a weekend movie night and it arrived two days earlier than expected. The case came sealed in a sturdy mailer with no cracks or dents, which is honestly rare these days. Disc was spotless and loaded up without any issues on my player. Picture quality is sharp and the sound mix really fills the room during the big set pieces. I went in with mixed expectations based on everything people said online, but the first hour actually pulled me in pretty quickly. Some of the editing choices are a bit jarring and the pacing drags in spots, but overall it looked great on my setup. Glad I picked up the physical copy instead of just streaming it. Solid addition to the shelf.

This movie is not easy to sit through but I'm really glad I watched it. The acting felt authentic and the story doesn't hold back from showing some pretty heavy realities. I found myself thinking about it for days afterwards. The pacing does drag a bit in the middle and some of the dialogue feels a little clunky but the emotional impact is undeniable. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who likes films that tackle real social issues without sugarcoating them. It's a good pick for book clubs or discussion groups since there's so much to unpack. Just don't expect a lighthearted watch, maybe save it for when you're in the right headspace. Four stars because it's powerful and eye-opening even with a few minor flaws.

I picked this up on sale and honestly, for what I paid, it's a decent watch. The colonial Australia setting is pretty unique and they clearly spent money on the locations and wardrobe. It looks great visually. My issue is the pacing really drags in the middle episodes. I found myself checking my phone a lot during episode 4 and almost gave up. The cast does a solid job but some of the character arcs feel rushed while others go nowhere. At full price I'd probably be more annoyed, but for around ten bucks it's a fair deal if you're into historical dramas and have patience for slow burns. Not something I'd rewatch but I don't regret buying it either. Just manage your expectations on the storytelling front.

Watched this over three nights and honestly couldn't wait to get back to it each evening. At over three hours it sounds like a commitment, but the pacing pulls you right through. Beatty completely disappears into Reed, you forget you're watching a movie star. The chemistry between him and Keaton feels raw and messy in the best way. Nicholson's small but memorable turn as O'Neill cracked me up. What surprised me most was how relevant the political arguments still feel today. The Russian Revolution sequences are genuinely epic without feeling like a textbook. Stapleton absolutely wrecks you in her scenes. Grabbed the Blu-ray and the transfer looks fantastic for a film from '81. Already planning a rewatch with friends.

Picked this up on sale and honestly it's worth every penny. You get nearly three hours of really ambitious filmmaking that weaves six completely different storylines together. Sure, some of the makeup choices are a little questionable and it can feel disjointed at times, but the scope of what they attempted is pretty incredible. The cast plays multiple roles across different time periods and some of the transformations are wild. The Blu-ray transfer looks fantastic on a decent TV and the special features give you a good chunk of behind the scenes stuff that explains how they pulled it all off. For what I paid, getting this much entertainment plus bonus content is a solid deal. Not a perfect movie by any stretch but definitely one that sticks with you.

Picked up the complete first season on Blu-ray for under fifteen bucks, which is a steal for eighteen episodes of this caliber. The real-time format keeps every hour moving at breakneck speed, and Kiefer Sutherland owns the role of Bauer completely. My only gripe is that the subplot involving his daughter Kim gets pretty ridiculous around the halfway mark, which drags things down a bit. Still, the main terrorist storyline is gripping enough that you will want to binge the whole thing over a weekend. Picture quality is solid for a show that aired in the early 2000s, and there are enough bonus features to justify the purchase. For the price they are asking now, you really cannot go wrong. Great bang for your buck.

I didn't expect much going in since most TV movie thrillers tend to be pretty forgettable, but this one genuinely surprised me. The story builds slowly at first and I almost gave up after the first twenty minutes, but I'm really glad I stuck with it. The tension ramps up beautifully and by the second half I was completely hooked. David Tennant is incredibly convincing in this role, honestly a bit unsettling how well he plays the character. The pacing could've been tighter in a few spots, but overall it's a solid watch that keeps you guessing. Way better than the typical made-for-TV fare I'm used to stumbling across on streaming. If you enjoy psychological dramas that don't spell everything out right away, give this a go.

Watched this with my teenager last weekend and we were both cracking up the entire time. Bateman plays this total slacker who figures out he can still compete in a national spelling bee because he never actually finished middle school. The concept sounds ridiculous but somehow it works perfectly. The kid actors are great and you genuinely feel for them when this grown man starts dominating their competition. Hahn is hilarious as the journalist tagging along for the ride, and there's a real sweetness underneath all the comedy. My son actually asked to watch it again the next day. Highly recommend for families with older kids, anyone who enjoys Bateman's deadpan style, or really anyone needing a feel-good laugh. Way better than I expected going in.

Got this on Blu-ray for under ten bucks and honestly that's a steal for what you get. The picture quality is way better than I expected - those shots of an empty London look incredibly sharp on a good TV. Murphy carries the whole thing pretty convincingly and the infected scenes still hold up after all these years. My only real gripe is the third act drags a bit once they reach the military base. Could've trimmed maybe fifteen minutes and had a tighter film. The commentary track and alternate endings are worth checking out too, so you're getting plenty of bonus content for the price. Not perfect but for what I paid I'm more than satisfied. Definitely worth grabbing if you see it cheap.

I'm so glad I picked this up on Blu-ray after missing it during its limited theatrical run. We made a whole family movie night out of it, and honestly, I wasn't sure how my teenagers would respond to Shakespeare, but they were completely drawn in from the opening scene. The performances are top-notch and the cinematography is just gorgeous. Everything feels grand but still intimate enough to connect with emotionally. We ended up pausing it twice just to talk about what was happening, which rarely happens in this house. The picture quality on the disc is crisp and the sound mix is excellent. If you've been on the fence about grabbing a copy, just do it. It's the kind of film you'll want to revisit more than once.

Got this on sale for five bucks and honestly that's about what it's worth. The story itself is pretty out there and hard to take seriously, but the performances are decent enough to keep you watching. I didn't hate it but I wouldn't watch it again either. At full price I'd say skip it, but if you catch it discounted it's an okay way to kill an hour and a half on a slow weeknight. Production quality is fine, nothing cheap looking, and the soundtrack is actually pretty good. Just don't expect anything profound or believable. It's the kind of movie that would have been fine as a lifetime original but tries to be more serious than it needs to be. Wait for a price drop.

Paid twelve bucks for this on Blu-ray and honestly I want my money back. I've sat through some slow films before but at least those had something to say. This just drags and drags with no payoff whatsoever. The trailer makes it look way more interesting than it actually is, which is basically nothing happening for two hours straight. I kept waiting for it to get better and it never did. Even the acting felt flat and uninspired, like nobody involved cared either. For the price they're charging you'd think there'd be at least some decent bonus features but nope, just the bare minimum. Could've rented this for three bucks and still felt ripped off. Don't waste your cash on this one. Total disappointment from start to finish.

Picked this up on sale and it's a decent watch if you don't expect too much going in. The cattle drive scenes are genuinely impressive and the scenery alone makes it worth the discounted price I paid. Rory Calhoun does fine in the lead, though the story itself feels pretty borrowed from older gaucho literature, like they took those classic themes and repackaged them for a Hollywood audience without really making them their own. Gene Tierney looks great but doesn't get a whole lot to do beyond that. At full retail I'd probably be more critical, but for around five bucks it's a fair deal for a lazy Sunday afternoon. Nothing groundbreaking, but the transfer quality is solid and the runtime moves along at a good pace.

Saw this opening weekend and my whole family was glued to the screen the entire time. The scale of destruction is honestly jaw-dropping, every time the creature shows up you feel it in your chest. What surprised me most was how much I actually cared about the characters. Usually in these types of films they're just forgettable placeholders running around, but the cast really sells the panic and desperation. The pacing moves fast without feeling rushed, and the third act delivers everything you'd want from a big monster feature. Sound design is incredible too, so watch it with good speakers if you can. My teenager has already asked to rewatch it twice. Definitely grabbing the Blu-ray when it drops. Just an all-around fun ride that exceeded my expectations.

I kept putting this off because silent-era Italian neorealism sounded like homework. Man, was I wrong. This hit me harder than pretty much anything I've watched this year. The premise sounds almost too simple, guy needs his bike to keep his job, bike gets stolen, he and his kid search Rome for it, but that simplicity is exactly what makes it devastating. You're not watching actors perform. You're watching real people barely scraping by, and every setback feels personal. The kid following his dad through the streets wrecked me, especially near the end. I expected something dry and academic I'd respect more than enjoy. Instead I got something raw and immediate that hasn't aged a day. Glad I finally took the plunge.

I went in expecting something sensationalized but was genuinely surprised by how restrained the filmmaking is. The thing I really appreciated was the cinematography, the Pacific Northwest setting is shot beautifully, and there's this haunting, almost dreamlike quality to the rural landscapes that mirrors the isolation these men clearly felt. It adds a melancholy layer without telling you how to feel. My one gripe is the pacing drags hard in the middle third. They could have cut about fifteen minutes and the emotional impact would've hit harder. Still, the interviews are handled with incredible sensitivity, and the aftermath of the incident is devastating to watch unfold. Not something I'd revisit, but it stuck with me for days. Definitely worth a watch if you can stomach the subject matter.

Ordered this on a whim during a late night movie browse. Shipping was pretty quick, showed up in about three days. The case arrived with a small crack on the front though, which was kind of a bummer since it was sold as new. Disc itself played fine with no skipping issues. First impression watching the opening scenes was that the production value looked decent for what it is. The storyline is predictable but has its moments. Honestly I expected a bit more based on the description. Not terrible for a lazy weekend watch but nothing I'd rush to recommend to friends either. Would probably rent it next time instead of buying. Three stars feels fair given the damaged case and the just-okay movie quality.

I'll give it three stars because the cinematography is genuinely impressive. The way they shot the time loop sequences with those subtle visual cues in the background really caught my attention. Every time a reset happened, there were tiny changes in the lighting and set dressing that most people probably wouldn't even notice. That said, the story itself drags hard in the second act. The main character keeps making the same dumb decisions over and over and it gets frustrating watching him ignore obvious solutions. The supporting cast is fine but nobody really gets enough development to matter. It's the kind of movie that looks great on a nice TV but falls apart if you think about the plot for more than five minutes. Worth a rental if you're bored.

I figured this would be just another throwaway thriller, but it genuinely caught me off guard. The pacing is tight from the opening scene and never really lets up. What surprised me most is how much weight the quieter moments carry, there's a scene about halfway through where two characters just talk, and it hit me harder than any of the action did. The performances across the board are solid, especially the lead, who sells every bit of desperation without overdoing it. I watched it on a weeknight expecting to zone out half-distracted on my phone, and instead I didn't touch the thing once. Ended up recommending it to my brother the next morning. If you're on the fence, just hit play. Way better than the trailer suggests.

I expected a fun, cheesy horror flick based on the description, but this was honestly painful to sit through. The acting is wooden across the board, and the storyline makes zero sense, characters just show up places with no explanation and the plot jumps around constantly. There are way too many drawn-out slow motion scenes that feel like obvious padding to reach a normal runtime. The special effects look like they were done on someone's laptop from 2002. I don't mind low budget horror when there's some charm or effort behind it, but this felt lazy and thrown together. Even by B-movie standards it's a slog. Wanted to like it, but ended up fast forwarding through the last thirty minutes just to be done with it.

I'll be honest, I had high hopes for this one given the cast of classic literary figures thrown together. Sean Connery does his best with what he's given, but the script is a mess and the CGI has aged like milk. The plot lurches from one explosion to another without ever making you care about what's happening. I watched it with my brother who loves cheesy early 2000s blockbusters and even he was checking his phone halfway through. That said, I'd actually recommend this to fans of so-bad-it's-good movies, there's enough nonsensical action and over-the-top moments to make for a fun riff night with friends. Just don't go in expecting anything coherent or faithful to the source material. Two stars for the camp value alone.

Ordered this on a whim after a friend wouldn't stop talking about it. Shipped super fast, arrived two days earlier than expected, and the case was in pristine condition. No cracks, no dented corners, which is honestly rare these days. The slipcover had that crisp, untouched feel. Popped it in the Blu-ray player the same evening and was hooked within the first ten minutes. The transfer looks sharp and the audio mix is clean. I didn't know much going in, which I think helped. Just a genuinely solid film that sneaks up on you emotionally. The performances feel raw without being overdone. Honestly glad I grabbed a physical copy instead of just streaming it somewhere. Already lent it to my neighbor and she texted me about it the next morning.

I've had this Blu-ray for about three years now and it still plays flawlessly. The disc has been through quite a few movie nights and hasn't picked up any scratches or freezing issues, which says something given how cheaply some older catalog titles are pressed. The restoration holds up well on repeat viewings. Black levels are deep and consistent, and the grain structure looks natural rather than smeared. My only real complaint is the extras feel a bit thin. There's a decent making-of piece but I was hoping for more on the production design since the entire thing was shot on one set. The case arrived intact and the cover art hasn't faded or peeled. Solid pickup if you're building a Hitchcock collection.

This series keeps getting better with every episode. The world-building is incredible and the characters feel so real. Balsa is easily one of the best female leads in anime, she is tough but also genuinely caring. The animation is gorgeous throughout and the soundtrack pulls you right into the story. I love how the show balances quiet emotional moments with real tension and action. The storylines involving the spirit world and the political intrigue keep me hooked every time. My whole family ended up watching it together and even my kids were invested in what happened next. If you enjoy fantasy with actual depth and character development, this is absolutely worth picking up. Already planning to rewatch the whole thing.

I'd only recommend this to film students who need to suffer through it for a class, or pretentious cinephiles who enjoy bragging about watching "challenging" cinema. Everyone else should skip it. I sat down expecting something provocative given the hype around Bardot, but what I got was a tedious, self-indulgent mess that mistakes incoherence for depth. The famous nude scene everyone talks about? Boring and completely devoid of any emotional weight. The dialogue goes in circles, the pacing is nonexistent, and I genuinely didn't care about a single character on screen. I love French New Wave as much as the next person, but this feels like Godard trolling his audience while pretending it's art. Save your money and your evening. Total waste of time.

I put off watching this for years because of all the mixed opinions, but I'm glad I finally sat down with it. Tom Cruise actually delivers one of his more vulnerable performances here, and Cameron Diaz is genuinely unsettling in her role. The first half hooked me completely with its dreamlike atmosphere and unpredictable tone shifts. Where it loses me a bit is the final act, when everything gets explained somewhat heavy-handedly. A little more ambiguity would've served the story better. Still, the soundtrack is incredible and the pacing keeps you engaged the whole way through. Not a casual weekend watch by any means, but if you're in the mood for something that makes you think and pays attention to detail, it's worth your time.

This special is exactly what I needed this December. The celebrity cameos are great and all, but the real standout for me is the musical arrangements. They somehow managed to take these ridiculous holiday songs and make them sound genuinely good while still being completely absurd. The duet with Willie Nelson had me rewinding three times because I couldn't stop laughing at how perfectly executed the whole bit was. The set design is another thing worth mentioning, it's got this deliberate retro variety show aesthetic that nails the 70s vibe without feeling like a cheap parody. My only minor complaint is that I wanted more Stephen Colbert, but what we got was gold. Already planning to make this a yearly tradition.

I've had this DVD in my collection for probably fifteen years now and it still plays perfectly despite being loaned out to friends and family more times than I can count. The disc has held up amazingly well with just basic care. As for the movie itself, it's a nice change of pace from Seagal's usual tough guy routine. He actually plays a character with some depth here, an environmentalist doctor standing up against corporate greed. The scenery alone makes it worth watching, but the story has stuck with me over the years too. Sure, it's not the nonstop action some people expect, but that's kind of what makes it special. Still holds up after all these years.

I've had this DVD for about three years now and it still plays perfectly despite being watched dozens of times. My kids aren't exactly gentle with discs and this one has survived more than a few careless handlings without a single skip or glitch. The picture quality holds up beautifully on our newer TV too, no weird graininess or compression issues like some older dance recordings get. I originally bought it after taking adult ballet classes locally and wanting to revisit some of the classic performances I'd read about. The extras and behind-the-scenes footage are genuinely interesting, not just filler. Packaging is sturdy enough that the case hasn't cracked like so many do. Absolutely worth every penny if you care about ballet history at all.

I grew up watching reruns of the original show, so I had pretty high hopes for this. Honestly, it's not as bad as everyone made it out to be, but it's also not great. Johnny Depp basically plays Jack Sparrow with face paint, which got old about halfway through. Armie Hammer is fine but feels a bit generic. The action scenes are over the top in that typical Jerry Bruckheimer way, lots of explosions and train chases that go on way too long. I expected more backstory and less slapstick comedy. The runtime is a real problem too. Could've easily been 30 minutes shorter. Watched it once and probably won't again. Decent popcorn movie if your expectations are low enough.

Save your money on this one. I rented this digitally for $6 and honestly feel robbed. The entire thing is basically people wandering around with shaky cameras whispering at each other for 90 minutes. Nothing remotely scary happens until maybe the last 10 minutes, and even that was underwhelming. I've seen better production value on YouTube for free. My girlfriend literally fell asleep halfway through and I don't blame her. The hype around this movie is completely baffling to me. If you're curious, just wait until it hits a free streaming service. Paying rental fees for this is throwing cash straight in the garbage. I want my $6 and those two hours of my life back. Complete and total ripoff.

The camera work in this is genuinely stunning - I'll give it that. Sweeping shots of mountains, oceans, deserts, all in gorgeous high definition. But whoever decided Michael York should narrate this clearly never listened to the final mix. His delivery is so overly dramatic and breathy it feels like a parody of a nature documentary. Every sentence is loaded with this heavy-handed gravitas that completely ruins the peaceful vibe the visuals are going for. I tried pushing through hoping it would calm down, but by the twenty minute mark I couldn't take it anymore. Had to switch to subtitles just to enjoy the scenery without the audio driving me up the wall. Save your money and just watch it muted with your own music playing.

I grabbed this expecting another low-budget creature feature with rubber ears and bad CGI, but man was I dead wrong. The practical effects alone are worth the price, there's a scene about forty minutes in that had me literally pausing to check if what I saw was real. The two leads have genuine chemistry, which is rare for indie horror where everyone seems like they're reading off cue cards. The pacing moves quick without feeling rushed, and the kills are creative without being gimmicky. My only complaint is the audio mix gets muddy during the outdoor sequences, had to crank my soundbar way up. If you're tired of mainstream horror playing it safe, this one actually swings for the fences. Already pre-ordered Ferrin's other stuff after finishing this.

I read Kurson's book years ago and wasn't sure how a documentary could capture that same tension, but this really delivers. What impressed me most was the underwater footage, they didn't just rely on talking heads and archival photos. Seeing Chatterton and Kohler actually back in the water, going through the process of identifying the U-boat, gives you a real sense of how grueling and dangerous those dives were. The cold, the low visibility, the equipment failures, it all comes through. My only minor complaint is I wished they spent a bit more time on the identity mystery itself, since the book goes deeper into the research side. But honestly, for a documentary adaptation, this is about as good as it gets. Watched it twice already.

I'd been meaning to watch this for years and finally grabbed it on a whim. Man, what a ride. Nicholson is at peak unpredictability here, every scene feels like it could go off the rails at any second, and I mean that in the best way. The road trip stuff in the first half is funny and uncomfortable in equal measure, and then the family dynamics later on just gut you. Karen Black is incredible too, equal parts annoying and heartbreaking. The dinner table sequence is one of those scenes I had to rewind immediately. The whole thing just has this raw, messy energy that movies today completely lack. Beautiful transfer on this edition too, looks way better than I expected for something from 1970. Absolutely worth owning.

I picked this up expecting the usual low-budget creature feature and that's basically what you get. The practical effects aren't terrible and some of the supporting performances are surprisingly solid. Ving Rhames does his thing and Lesley-Ann Brandt holds her own in the action scenes. But man, Taryn Manning is genuinely painful to watch here. Every line delivery feels like a first table read and her character adds absolutely nothing to the plot. I kept waiting for her to get written out but no such luck. The story itself is thin even by made-for-TV standards. I'd only recommend this to die-hard zombie completists who literally have nothing else queued up. Everyone else should probably skip it and rewatch something better.

Got this DVD about four months ago and honestly it's already showing major wear issues. The disc started skipping around the two month mark and now halfway through the film it just freezes up completely. I always keep my DVDs in their cases and handle them by the edges, so this isn't on me. The layer seems incredibly thin compared to other older westerns in my collection. Even the case itself arrived with a cracked hinge on one side and now the front cover won't stay shut properly. The movie itself is a decent Audie Murphy western with some good action sequences, but what good is that if you can't actually watch the whole thing? Pretty disappointed with how flimsy this pressing feels. Expected better longevity for the price.

Picked this up mostly for The Phantom Light and wasn't disappointed. The Welsh coastal setting is genuinely atmospheric, you really get a sense of isolation and creeping dread around that lighthouse. The fog sequences look surprisingly effective for the era. My only real gripe is the print quality isn't exactly restored to perfection. There are noticeable scratches and some contrast issues in the darker scenes, which is a shame when the mood is so dependent on shadow work. Still, the storytelling holds up remarkably well and the pacing doesn't waste your time. The second film on the disc is decent too, though I found myself wanting to revisit the lighthouse story more. For the price it's hard to complain too loudly. Solid collection overall.

I've had this DVD for about eight months now and it's held up great despite being loaned out to three different friends and watched probably a dozen times. No scratches, no skipping, the disc still plays clean every time. The case hasn't cracked either which is more than I can say for most stuff ordered online lately. The documentary itself is well put together and walks through everything in a way that's easy to follow even if you're not deep into this stuff. My only gripe is some sections feel a bit repetitive and could've been trimmed down. Overall though it's a solid watch and the physical media quality is genuinely impressive. Would definitely recommend picking it up if you want something that'll last in your collection.

Ordered the Blu-ray version and it arrived two days earlier than expected, which was a nice surprise. The case was in pristine condition with zero cracks or dents, they actually shipped it in a sturdy mailer with bubble wrap, not one of those flimsy envelopes that ruin everything. Slipped the disc in right away and the transfer looks sharper than I remember from my old DVD copy. Sound mix is solid too. Honestly forgot how many iconic lines are packed into this thing. The special features are decent, nothing mind-blowing, but the behind-the-scenes stuff is worth a watch if you're a fan. For the price point this is a no-brainer pickup. Already lent it to my coworker who's never seen it.

I expected this to be completely unwatchable as an adult, but it actually holds up better than most 80s teen comedies. The telekinesis gags are way more creative than I remembered, and Baio actually commits to the absurdity. My buddy put it on during a nostalgia movie night and I figured we'd last maybe twenty minutes before switching to something else. Ended up watching the whole thing. Yeah, the pacing drags in the middle and some jokes have aged terribly, but there's an earnestness here that newer raunchy comedies completely lack. The prom scene alone is worth the price. Not quite as funny as I thought it was at fourteen, but way less embarrassing than I feared. Solid four stars for the nostalgia factor.

I went into this expecting pretty much unwatchable cheese, so I was genuinely surprised by how entertaining it turned out. The production values are decent for a 1950s sci-fi flick, and the whole secret lab setup with the robots actually creates some real tension. No, it's not going to blow you away with deep themes or groundbreaking effects, but the pacing moves along nicely and the acting is more competent than you'd expect from something this obscure. My only real complaint is that the middle section drags a bit before the payoff. The print quality on this release isn't amazing either, but honestly for what it is, it's perfectly watchable. If you're into cold war era sci-fi and have reasonable expectations, you'll probably enjoy this more than you think.

Ordered the complete series box set and it arrived two days earlier than expected. Packaging was solid - no dented corners or crushed edges, which is always a relief with collector sets. Everything inside was pristine. Popped in the first disc immediately and the video quality is noticeably better than what I remember watching on TV years back. The menus are clean and easy to navigate, no annoying forced previews to sit through either. Each season has its own slim case with original artwork, and they slide neatly into the outer box without feeling cheap or flimsy. I'd forgotten how quickly this show hooks you right from the pilot. Already four episodes deep on night one. Totally worth grabbing if you've been on the fence about owning physical copies.

Ordered this Blu-ray after wanting to revisit it for years. Shipping was surprisingly fast, arrived two days earlier than expected. The case arrived in perfect condition with no cracks or dents, which is always a relief ordering media online. Disc was secure in the spindle and spotless right out of the wrapper. Popped it in the same night and the transfer looks really sharp for a film from the early 2000s. Kinnear completely nails the role and the whole thing has this unsettling, voyeuristic tone that sticks with you. Only knocking off a star because the special features are pretty thin, would've loved a retrospective documentary or something. Solid release overall though and worth picking up if you're a fan of the cast or the director.

I've had this Blu-ray for about three years now and it's held up really well. My kids have watched it probably twenty times and the disc still plays without any skipping or buffering issues. The steelbook case I got has survived multiple moves and still looks great on the shelf with minimal scuffing. The movie itself is a fun watch. The creature designs are genuinely creative and the 1920s New York setting works well. I will say the plot meanders a bit in the second act and some of the supporting characters feel underdeveloped compared to the leads. But the visual effects hold up on repeat viewings and the soundtrack is fantastic through a decent sound system. Solid addition to the collection overall.

Ordered the Blu-ray on a Tuesday and it showed up by Thursday which was a nice surprise. Packaging was solid, no cracked cases or bent artwork, just a secure mailer with bubble wrap inside. The disc had zero scratches and played perfectly from start to finish on my player. First viewing was a wild ride honestly. The pacing throws you right in and the visual style is super vibrant throughout. Some of the story threads felt a little underdeveloped and I wished a couple characters got more screen time but overall it kept me hooked the entire runtime. The audio mix is fantastic if you have a decent sound setup. Definitely worth picking up if you enjoy gritty crime dramas with a distinct flair.

Ordered this Glenn Ford western last Tuesday and it arrived by Friday, way faster than I expected. The packaging was solid, they actually used a sturdy mailer with bubble wrap inside, so no cracked cases or scratched discs. The shrink-wrap was intact and the cover art looked sharp, not some cheap reprint. Popped it in right away and the transfer is honestly better than I anticipated for a lesser-known title. Colors looked natural and the audio was clean throughout. I've been hunting down Ford's westerns for a while now and this one slipped under my radar for years. Really glad I finally grabbed a copy. First impression straight out of the box was that whoever shipped this actually cared. Five stars all around.

Bought this Blu-ray about eight months ago and it's been played a ton since then. My kids are obsessed with Spider-Man so this gets popped into the player at least once a week. The disc has held up perfectly despite being handled by little hands, no scratches, no skipping, no issues at all. The case itself is still in great shape too, which honestly surprises me given how careless my boys can be. The movie itself is fantastic. The animation looks incredible on our living room TV, and the story actually hits hard emotionally every single time. Even after watching it probably thirty plus times I still catch little background details I missed before. Absolutely worth picking up if you want something the whole family will rewatch endlessly.
